steps: Soften cream cheese and then mix all ingredients together except 2 tbsp cheddar cheese. Place mixture into casserole and top with remaining cheese.
Bake 350° 30 minutes and serve with bread or crackers.

items: 1 Lb of skinless, boneless chicken breasts, chopped
1 brick of cream cheese, softened at room temperature
½ bottle of prepared, [blue cheese dressing](recipe:blue-cheese-dressing)
Frank’s Hot Sauce or other buffalo hot sauce, to taste

steps: Preheat oven to 350F.

Mix the cream cheese, [blue cheese dressing](recipe:blue-cheese-dressing) and Frank’s hot sauce in a bowl until well combined. Add in chopped chicken and put in casserole or other oven proof bowl. Add blue cheese and scallions to top, if using.
Bake in oven until ingredients and cheese have melted and chicken is cooked through. Serve warm with chips and celery.

items: 2-4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, halved and pounded flat

steps: Preheat over to 350F. Put French’s Fried Onions and flour in plastic bag and beat until it looks like a breading mixture.
Dip chicken into egg; then coat with onion crumbs on both sides, pressing firmly to adhere. Place chicken on baking sheet.
Bake breaded chicken 20 to 25 minutes minutes or until golden brown and cooked through.

ingredient_groups.name: For the Kebabs
items: 2 tablespoons ground Urfa pepper flakes, divided

steps: For the Kebabs: Combine lamb with 7.5 grams (about 2 teaspoons) kosher salt, 1 teaspoon cumin, 2 teaspoons sumac, and 1 tablespoon pepper flakes. Knead by hand or in a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment until mixture turns tacky and starts sticking to the side of the bowl. Add water and continue kneading until incorporated. Place in refrigerator and chill well.

Meanwhile, combine remaining teaspoon cumin, 2 teaspoons sumac, remaining tablespoon pepper flakes, and 2 teaspoons salt in a small bowl. Set spice mixture aside. Combine remaining 2 teaspoons sumac and red onions in a medium bowl. Season with salt to taste and set aside.
Using wet hands, divide lamb mixture into 12 even balls. Using wet hands, form each ball into a long, flat kebab around a skewer.

Light one chimney full of charcoal. When all the charcoal is lit and covered with gray ash, pour out and arrange the coals on one side of the charcoal grate. Set cooking grate in place, cover grill and allow to preheat for 5 minutes. Alternatively, set half the burners on a gas grill to the highest heat setting, cover, and preheat for 10 minutes. Clean and oil the grilling grate. Place kebabs directly over hot side of grill, cover, and cook, turning occasionally and sprinkling with spice mixture until well charred on both sides and kebabs are cooked through, about 12 minutes total.
During last few minutes of cooking, place bread directly on top of kebabs in batches until heated through. Serve kebabs with warm bread, sumac onions, parsley, tomatoes, and pickled peppers.

items: 500 g all purpose flour King Arthur brand is recommended about 3 1/2 cups, using 'scoop and swipe' method
3 g instant yeast about 1 tsp; also known as Quick Rise or Rapid Rise yeast

steps: Mix all ingredients in a bowl, cover with a plastic wrap and let rest for 15 minutes. Over a period of 1 1/2 hours, do 3 sets of stretch and folds, flipping the dough upside down after each set. Cover the bowl with a plastic wrap and place in refrigerator overnight for about 12-14 hours. Turn the dough on a lightly floured work surface. Divide into 3 equal parts and shape into rectangles. Cover and let rest for 45-60 minutes.
Starting preheating the oven to 500F, with a baking stone positioned in the upper half the oven and a bread pan filled with hot water on the bottom rack.
Stretch each dough rectangle slightly and fold into a cylinder, sealing the seams. Using your hands, roll the cylinders gently stretching them to desired length, about 14-15 inches.

Place on a lightly floured couche, seam side up. Cover and proof at a room temperature for about 30-60 minutes, or until the dough has sufficiently proofed.
Transfer the baguettes to a piece of parchment paper, seam side down and dust off excess flour. Using a bread lame, a sharp knife or a razor blade, make 3 scores on each baguette. When scoring, use a swift and firm motion to ensure nice and clean cuts.
Open the oven, taking caution not to get burned by steam, and slide the baguettes off onto the baking stone. Close the oven and reduce temperature to 475F. Bake for 15 minutes.
Remove the water pan, rotate the baguettes, drop the temperature to 450F and continue baking for another 15 minutes or until deep golden brown.

items: 1 to 1 & 1/2 lb. fish (typically salmon or firm white fish)
⅛ to ¼ cup of white wine (optional)
Herbs such as parsley, basil, or cilantro
Easy pre-made seasoning such as cajun, curry, chile powder, or other spice mix

steps: Preheat oven to 400F or 350F. The lower temperature will cook the fish slower, but will result in more succulent final product. If you have the time, the lower temperature is better.

Look at fillet. If the cut has uneven thickness, consider cutting in half, so you can take the thinner half out when it is done. Decide if you are going to cook in a roasting pan or “papillote” (parchment paper or tin foil packet). In a packet, you will get less browning but hopefully more succulent fish. Season fish with olive oil, salt and pepper, and any seasoning rub. Place in cooking vessel and dress with any herbs and lemon slices and place any butter on top. Put any wine cooking vessel.

Put in oven. Start checking temperature with an instant read thermometer in 10 minutes. 145F is medium. It should take 15 to 20 minutes to cook, but could take longer or shorter depending on oven and cut. If you want to get fancy, you can broil fish in a roasting pan to brown the top (1 to 2 minutes) and then finish in the oven at 400F. You should stay near the fish the entire time it is broiling, to ensure you don’t burn it. Serve with a simple vegetable side and, if desired, potatoes.

sections.name: Watercress Sauce for Fish

items: 8 Tbs parsley, about ½ a bunch (or 4 Tbs of parsley and 4 Tbs of mint)
Juice from half a lemon (or more, to taste)

steps: Chop everything in a food processor. Slowly add olive oil, until you achieve the consistency you want. I prefer this to be chunky, instead of a more viscous green sauce. Check the seasoning, adding black pepper and lemon juice as you think fit, but no salt. Stir in hemp seeds when the sauce is removed from the food processor. The sauce should have a bright, salty-fruity-lemony flavour to it.

items: 1/4 Tsp baking soda (optional, helps quickly break down onions)
1 to 6 green chilies (to taste), roughly chopped
2 14 oz cans chickpeas, drained and rinsed (or other vegetables or protein)
1 cup cilantro leaves, about a whole bunch, roughly chopped

steps: Combine garlic, ginger, chilies, half of lemon juice, and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt in a mortar and pestle or in the small work bowl of a food processor and pound or process until a fine paste is produced. Instead of that, you can also just finely mince everything together (this is what I usually do.) Set aside.

Heat oil in a large saucepan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add onion all at once, along with baking soda, if using. Cook, stirring frequently, until onions start to leave a brown coating on bottom of pan, 3 to 4 minutes. Add 1 tablespoon water, scrape up browned bits from pan, and continue cooking. If you have time or the patience, repeat this process until onions are a deep brown, about 10 minutes total.

Immediately add garlic/ginger/chili paste all at once and stir to combine. Add coriander, black pepper, turmeric, and 1 teaspoon garam masala. Stir until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add tomatoes and crush them using a whisk or potato masher. Add drained, rinsed chickpeas and cilantro, reserving a little cilantro for garnish. Add 1/2 cup water.

Bring to a simmer, cover with lid slightly cracked, and reduce heat to maintain a gentle bubbling. Cook, stirring occasionally, until liquid has reduced into a thick stew and spices have melded, about 30 minutes.
Stir in remaining garam masala and lemon juice. Season to taste with salt. Serve with rice and/or naan, sprinkling additional cilantro on top.

notes.name: Variations
notes.text: substitute for chickpeas (or in addition to chickpeas), roasted cauliflower/broccoli, pressed and baked tofu (see [Tofu Stir Fry](recipe:tofu-stir-fry) for technique), spinach, kale, swiss chard, shrimp or chicken (saute first to brown and so chicken can cook through in sauce).

sections.name: Coconut Milk Variation

ingredient_groups.name: Additional Ingredients
items: 1 tsp. sugar (any type, but brown is preferred)
1 medium tomato, diced (omit if using cherry tomatoes as well)
1 1/2 cups coconut water or broth (vegetable or chicken), as needed
14-ounce package of extra firm tofu, drained well

Vegetables, such as carrots, shallots, red bell pepper, mushrooms, zucchini, cherry tomatoes, greens (mustard or beet greens have worked really well for me), all chopped to approximately 1” long pieces or in chunks.
3 medium carrots, 1” thick sliced on a diagonal
1 red bell pepper, cut in 2” pieces

steps: Don’t use any chilis with the garlic/ginger paste. In a dutch oven over medium heat, warm the oil. Add the onion/shallots, garlic, ginger and salt and saute until softened but not browned. About 5 minutes. Add the cumin, curry powder, turmeric, sugar and saute another minute. Add the peanut butter, coconut milk, fish sauce (if using), tomatoes, chili paste and coconut water or broth and stir to mix. Let everything simmer on low for 15 minutes.

At this point, you can transfer sauce to a blender and run the blender to create a smooth sauce (and then return to pot.) I almost never do and it is fine. Stir in the lime juice. Taste for seasoning. It should be somewhat thick, but still thin enough that the vegetables will cook in it’s heat. Add more broth, coconut water, or plain water if needed.

Cut the tofu into 1” cubes and prepare all your vegetables. Add carrots, shallots, zucchini, or greens to the pot first and cook for 5 minutes, then add the tofu, bell pepper, or mushrooms and cook another 10-15 minutes until all the vegetables are just tender but not mushy.

items: 15 lbs of beef bone (neck bones are best)

steps: Preheat oven to 450. Toss bones with tomato paste and roast for 45 minutes until thoroughly browned.
Very roughly chop vegetables. Put roasted bones and vegetables into stock pot and add herbs. Cover with water - it may be very full.
Very gently simmer bones and vegetables overnight. Strain stock and let cool, then jar.

items: ½ head of small green cabbage, sliced
1 handful of prune, chopped into small bite-sized pieces

steps: Toss beef with flour and season with salt and pepper. Brown in a dutch oven in neutral oil. Reserve beef and discard the oil.
In the same dutch oven, saute onion with the bacon until softened and beginning to turn golden.
Meanwhile pre-heat the oven to 325 and bring a pot of water to boil. Boil the cabbage and the sauerkraut for 20 minutes.
Once the onion is softened, add in the beef, kielbasa and cooked cabbage and sauerkraut. Add in the prunes, mushrooms and thyme. Add in wine and simmer for five minutes, then add in the stock.
Braise the beef in the dutch oven in the oven covered for 2-3 hours until completely tender. Take the lid off the last 30-60 minutes to reduce liquid and brown, stirring occasionally.
In a small bowl, mix together all dressing ingredients. Stir until completely combined and set aside in refrigerator.

items: a splash of red wine or brandy
1 small can (7 oz) chipotle chili in adobo sauce (can use half a can for a less spicy version)
1 tablespoon ancho chili powder or Mexican chili powder
1 handful of cilantro leaves and stems

steps:
Heat a braising pot over medium heat and add olive oil. Season the beef with salt and pepper generously, and brown all around to sear in a pot. Remove the beef and set aside.
Add the onion, pepper, and saute for 5 minutes. Add garlic into the pot and saute for 2 more minutes. Splash with red wine or brandy and let it reduce.

Return the beef to the pot. Add the diced tomatoes, chili in adobo sauce (full or half-can), chili powder, cayenne pepper, bay leaf, and cilantro. Drizzle water over and cover. Simmer over low heat for 3 hours or braise in oven at 350F for 3 hours. Using a full can of chili in adobo sauce will produce a spicy taco with a strong chipotle taste. Use less as need to your taste.
Remove the beef to a cutting board and shred with forks. Place the shredded beef into a serving bowl and add some gravy left in a pot to the beef, mix well. Season with salt and pepper if needed.
Serve with tortilla and other toppings like guacamole, lettuce, tomatoes, cheese, etc.

items: Several dried chiles such as guajillo or ancho chiles, rehydrated in water and de-seeded and de-stemmed (optional)

steps: Season lamb shanks and then brown in a large saute pan on all sides in olive oil or other neutral oil.

Reserve shanks, add a tablespoon of additional oil if necessary, then saute onion, carrots, celery, and fennel, if using. Once the vegetables are softened, add tomato paste and garlic and saute another minute. Deglaze with wine and bring to a boil.
Add vegetables and wine to pressure cooker. Add lamb shanks and juices on top. Add in bay leaves, herbs, cinnamon and chiles (if using). Add vegemite and lemon rind.
Seal pressure cooker and then cook on high pressure (12 psi) for 50 minutes. Once lamb is done, strain out the vegetables from the gravy and serve with gremolata on the side

sections.name: Gremolata

items: Zest of 1 lemon, minus 1 strip reserved for lamb

steps: Mix parsley, lemon zest, and garlic. Serve gremolata as a topping for braised and roasted meat dishes such as lamb shank and osso bucco.
In the mixing bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment, whisk together 1 cup warm water, yeast, and sugar. Let stand until foamy, about 5 minutes.

To the yeast mixture, add 2 cups flour, and oil or butter. Beat on low speed until combined, about 1 minute. Slowly add the remaining ½ cup flour along with the salt. Increase the speed to medium and knead until a smooth and elastic dough is formed, about 6 minutes. (The dough will be slightly tacky but shouldn’t stick to a clean finger when tapped.)
Transfer the dough to a lightly greased large bowl, cover, and let rise in a warm place until doubled in size, about 45 minutes.
Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper.

Punch down the risen dough. On a lightly floured surface, divide the dough into 12 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a 9-inch rope and place on the prepared baking sheet about 2 inches apart. Cover and let rise in a warm place until visibly puffed, about 30 minutes.
Bake for 15 to 17 minutes or until golden brown. Remove from oven to cooling rack. Brush topping on breadsticks minutes after leaving oven.
Put brown rice and water in pressure cooker. Cook on PSI 12.0 (high pressure) for 15 minutes on the rice setting (or natural release).

title: Cabbage Slaw (For Fritters, Pancakes and Tacos)

items: 2 Tsp Sriracha or other chile sauce
1 Half head of cabbage, red or green, thinly sliced

steps: In a salad bowl combine all of the ingredients besides the cabbage and mix until evenly combined. Add cabbage and thoroughly coat. Serve slaw on top of zucchini, potato, or other fritters, pancakes, or tacos.

sections.name: Simple version
steps: Toss cabbage with ½ tsp salt, ½ tsp sugar, lime juice, and apple cider vinegar. Let it sit for half an hour in the fridge.

items: 2 and 1/2 cups (313g) all-purpose flour (spooned & leveled), plus more as needed for hands and work surface
1/2 cup (8 Tbsp; 113g) unsalted butter, cubed and very cold
1 teaspoon dried or fresh chopped parsley

steps: Preheat oven to 425°F (218°C).

Place the flour, baking powder, baking soda, garlic powder, and salt together in a large bowl or in a large food processor and whisk or pulse until combined. Add the cubed butter and cut into the dry ingredients with a pastry cutter or by pulsing several times in the processor until coarse crumbs form. (If you used a food processor, pour the mixture into a large bowl.) Fold in the shredded cheese.

Make a well in the center of the mixture. Pour 1 cup (240ml) buttermilk and drizzle honey on top. Fold everything together with a large spoon or spatula until it begins to come together—do not overwork the dough (it will be shaggy and crumbly with some wet spots).

Pour the dough and any dough crumbles onto a floured work surface and gently bring together with generously floured hands. Flatten into a 3/4-inch-thick rectangle, then fold one end in toward the center and the other end on top of that (like a business letter). Flatten back into a 3/4-inch-thick rectangle and repeat the folding and flattening process once more.
Flatten into a final 3/4-inch-thick rectangle and cut into 2.5- or 3-inch circles with a biscuit cutter, pressing straight down without twisting. Re-roll scraps until all the dough is used.
Arrange biscuits close together (touching) in a 10-inch cast iron skillet or on a parchment paper-lined baking sheet. Brush the tops with the remaining 2 tablespoons buttermilk.

Bake for 18–22 minutes or until tops are golden brown. Remove from the oven. Mix the 2 tablespoons of butter, garlic powder, and parsley together, generously brush on the warm biscuits, and serve warm.

items: 1 1/4 cups Marsala wine (use good quality, drinkable dry Marsala from Sicily)
1.75 - 2 lbs chicken cutlets/breast meat pounded to relatively even thickness
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
About 1 cup all-purpose flour, for dredging
Extra-virgin olive oil, approximately ¼ cup for sauteing chicken
10 ounces button mushrooms, stemmed and thinly sliced
White wine vinegar, sherry vinegar, or fresh lemon juice, to taste

steps: Combine Marsala and stock in a mixing bowl or large measuring cup and sprinkle gelatin all over surface. Set aside.

Season chicken cutlets all over with salt and pepper. Pour a roughly 1/2-inch layer of flour into a wide, shallow bowl. Dredge each cutlet in flour, tap off excess, and transfer to clean plate. Prep vegetables.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet (a traditional saute pan is the best) over medium-high heat until shimmering. Working in batches, add chicken and cook, turning once, until browned on both sides, about 2-3 minutes per side. Using a slotted spatula, transfer to paper towels to drain. You will finish the chicken in the sauce, so you just want to brown the chicken and not worry about cooking it all the way through. This will also keep the chicken very tender and avoid over-cooking. You will develop browned-bits (frond) on the bottom of the pan - this is normal and actually desirable.

After removing last pieces of chicken, add mushrooms to skillet (do not drain remaining oil) and cook, stirring frequently, until mushrooms have released their juices and browned well, about 10 minutes. If the pan is very dry, add 1-2 tablespoons of water with the mushrooms to avoid burning the frond or the mushrooms. Add shallots/onion, leeks, and thyme and cook, stirring, until shallots/onions and leeks are soft or translucent, about 2 minutes. Add garlic and saute for 30 more seconds.

Pour Marsala mixture into pan, making sure to scrape in all the gelatin. Bring to a boil, whisking and scraping up any browned bits from bottom of pan, until liquids are reduced by about about a half and the sauce no longer has a sharp taste from the alcohol in the wine. Add butter and soy sauce and stir constantly until emulsified and sauce takes on a consistency approaching that of heavy cream. Season with salt and pepper. Taste sauce and adjust with a small amount of vinegar or lemon juice, as needed.

Return chicken cutlets to pan, swirling to bathe them in the sauce and warm them through. If the sauce begins to break at any point, swirl in a splash of water to bring it back together. Transfer to a warmed serving plate, spooning sauce all over chicken. Garnish with parsley and serve.

items: 1 Lb of skinless, boneless chicken breasts chopped by hand (preferred for better texture and better quality of meat) or 1 lb ground chicken or
⅓ cup fresh lime juice, from about 2 limes
¾ cup thinly sliced shallots, about two shallots
1 thinly sliced hot chili such as Thai bird, Serrano, or jalapeño or more to taste
½ cilantro, mint or mixture of both (best), can be estimated by half of a bunch

steps: Place the chicken and 1/4 cup water in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook, stirring occasionally to break up any clumps of meat, until the chicken is cooked through, about 8 minutes—you don’t want to brown the chicken, so lower heat as needed.
Meanwhile, stir together the lime juice, fish sauce, and sugar in a small bowl, until the sugar is dissolved. Set aside.

Add scallions, shallots, and chili to skillet, and cook over low heat just until the vegetables are tender and most of the liquid has evaporated, 3 to 4 minutes. Remove from heat. Stir in the sauce, cilantro, and mint, and toss to coat.
Serve the larb with the lettuce leaves and rice on the side. You can make lettuce cups with rice and larb or serve everything together, which is a lot less messy but not traditional.

items: Baking powder, ¼ Tsp per pound of wings

steps: Line rimmed baking sheet with aluminum foil, and set rack inside. Carefully dry chicken wings with paper towels. Place wings in large bowl, sprinkle with baking powder and salt and pepper, and toss until thoroughly and evenly coated. Place on rack, leaving slight space between each wing.
Place baking sheet with wings in refrigerator and allow to rest, uncovered, at least 8 hours, and up to 18 hours.

Adjust oven rack to upper-middle position and preheat oven to 450°F or pre-heat broiler if possible. Add chicken wings to oven or place 1-2 inches below broiler and cook for 20 minutes. Flip wings and continue to cook until crisp and golden brown, 15 to 25 minutes longer.
Toss with sauce as desired and serve.

items: 1 tbsp smoked paprika (regular paprika is fine, but smoked has the best flavor)

steps: Mix everything together and store in a dark cupboard. Season chicken. This has no salt, so you can salt as desired.

title: Chickpea Bowl with Cauliflower and Fennel Salad

items: 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ medium head of cauliflower (about ¾ lb.), broken into large florets, sliced ¼" thick
1 medium fennel bulb, halved lengthwise, very thinly sliced crosswise
1 small chile, such as serrano, Frenso, or jalapeño (optional), thinly sliced

steps: Preheat oven to 400°. Mix garlic, coriander, cumin, and 3 Tbsp. oil in a large bowl. Add cauliflower and chickpeas; season with salt and pepper. Toss to coat.

Transfer cauliflower mixture to a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet. Wipe out bowl; reserve. Bake, tossing halfway through, until chickpeas and cauliflower are golden brown and cauliflower is tender, 18–22 minutes.
Meanwhile, mix yogurt, 1 Tbsp. lemon juice, and a big pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Toss fennel, chile (if using), parsley, sesame seeds, and remaining 3 Tbsp. lemon juice in a reserved bowl.
Spread yogurt mixture in serving bowls. Top with spiced chickpea mixture. Scatter fennel salad over, then drizzle with oil and toss with fennel/sesame seed mixture.

items: 1 14 oz can of chickpeas (drained and washed in colander)
A couple grated carrots or pre-shredded carrots (optional)
¼ cup of hummus, tahini, or mixture of two
Juice of 1 lemon, with some zest or without (optional)
1 Tbs of chopped fresh herbs (basil, rosemary, mint) (optional)
1-2 Tbs of sesame, hemp, chia, or ground flaxseeds

steps: Make this with any of the vegetables that you have around. Put everything into a mixing bowl and mash with a potato masher until a chunky spread is made. Top with spices, if desired. Refrigerate and use for easy vegan sandwiches (bread must be vegan).
Fry garlic, shallot, and chili flakes in oil for 5 minutes or until fragrant and chili flakes are browning. Watch out, the chili may burn your eyes!
Pour into mason jar and mix in other ingredients.

items: 1/3 of tops of scallion bunch, chopped
4 TBS (or more) Soy Sauce / Momofuku Soy Noodle Sauce

steps: Cook instant ramen according to directions and throw out broth packets.
Mix the rest of the ingredients together. When ramen is done, toss everything together.
Eat by itself or top with radishes, greens, eggs, shrimp, tofu, or anything else!
Add the bread flour and salt to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook attachment (or a large regular mixing bowl) and whisk together to incorporate.

Turn the mixer on low speed, and gradually add the water in two batches, giving the flour time to absorb the water with each addition. If doing this by hand, simply stir with your hands as you gradually add the water.
The mixture will eventually form a shaggy dough after 5 minutes of kneading. If the mixer fails to bring it all together, turn off the mixer and push the dough together with your hands.

Once the dough has formed a relatively cohesive ball (it will look lumpy), continue to knead by with the mixer for 10 minutes or by hand for 15 minutes. Avoid the temptation to add additional water, as this will affect the texture of your noodles.
Cover the dough with an overturned bowl, and allow it to rest for 30 minutes. During this time, it will continue to absorb moisture, and become more pliable and elastic.
After the dough has rested, knead it a few more times to get any air bubbles out of it. Form into a ball and cut the ball in half.
On a floured surface, roll one half of the dough into a thin sheet, about 2mm thick––this will take time! Flour the surface of the sheet thoroughly, flip over, and thoroughly flour the other side.

Once floured, fold the dough so you have 4 layers. Slice the noodles with a sharp knife to your desired thickness. We decided to cut them about ⅛-inch thick. As you’re cutting the noodles, gently separate them out with your hands and toss them in flour so they don’t stick. Repeat this process with the second half of the dough.

Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the noodles for 1 to 3 minutes, depending on the thickness. Keep an eye on the noodles as they cook and taste them to determine when they’re cooked (there is a lot of variation depending on how thinly they were rolled and cut, so test in real time to determine when they’re done). Serve in soup or with sauce as desired!

sources.text: Chinese Handmade Noodles: Just 3 Ingredients! - The Woks of Life

items: 1-2 loaves (about 1-2 pounds) good quality white or sourdough bread, cut into 3/4-inch cubes
1 pound bulk Italian pork sausage or standard breakfast sausage
2 medium carrots, peeled and finely chopped (optional)
1 tablespoon chopped fresh sage (or 1 teaspoon rubbed sage)
1/2 cup dry white wine or vermouth
2 to 4 cups low-sodium chicken or turkey broth
2 large eggs, lightly beaten Salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Spread the bread cubes in a single layer on two large rimmed baking sheets. Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, tossing halfway through, until dry and lightly toasted. Remove from oven and transfer to a very large mixing bowl.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up with a wooden spoon into small pieces, until browned and cooked through, about 6 to 8 minutes. Use a slotted spoon to transfer the cooked sausage to the bowl with the toasted bread, leaving the rendered fat in the skillet.

Add the butter to the skillet with the sausage fat over medium heat. Once melted, add the onions, celery, and carrots (if using). Season with salt and pepper and cook, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables are softened and the onions are translucent, about 8 to 10 minutes.

Add the garlic, sage, thyme, and rosemary to the skillet. Cook, stirring constantly, until fragrant, about 1 minute. Pour in the white wine to deglaze the pan, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, and cook until the wine is mostly reduced, about 3 to 4 minutes.
Pour the cooked vegetable and herb mixture over the bread and sausage in the large bowl. Toss everything together thoroughly.

In a small bowl, whisk together 2 cups of chicken broth and the beaten eggs. Pour the mixture over the stuffing and toss gently until the bread is evenly moistened. (If the mixture still looks dry or the bread isn't sufficiently hydrated, add up to 1 more cup of broth). Taste a small amount of the bread mixture and season with additional salt and pepper as needed.
Transfer the stuffing mixture to a greased 9x13-inch baking dish (or equivalent casserole dish). Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue baking for another 20 to 25 minutes, or until the top is golden brown and crisp. Remove from the oven, let rest for 10 minutes, and serve warm.

sources.text: Classic Sage and Sausage Stuffing (Dressing) Recipe

items: ½ lb cooking apples (peeled, cored and chopped small)
½ lb fresh or frozen cranberries (thawed if frozen)
¼ lb pitted dates (each date cut into 3)

steps: Add everything to a pan. Bring to a boil and then put on low simmer for approximately an hour until everything has collapsed into a chutney. Store in sterilized mason jars.

items: 1 pound white fish (such as cod, hake, or halibut), cut into eight 2-ounce fingers
2 quarts or so of oil for deep frying (preferably peanut oil)

steps: Combine flour, paprika, black pepper, and salt and whisk to combine. Transfer half of mixture to a large bowl and set aside. Add beer and egg to remaining mixture and whisk until a smooth batter is formed. Batter should have the consistency of thick paint (add up to 1/2 cup more beer as necessary until proper consistency is reached). Set aside.

Heat oil in a deep fryer, Dutch oven, or large wok to 350°F. Transfer fish pieces to bowl with batter and turn to coat thoroughly. Working one piece at a time, lift fish, let excess batter drip off, then transfer to bowl with remaining flour mixture. Toss to coat thoroughly. Lift carefully with tongs or dry fingers and slowly lower into hot oil. Repeat with remaining fish. You may have to fry in batches.
Fry, turning occasionally, until golden brown on all sides, about 3 minutes total. Transfer to a paper towel-lined plated and season with salt.

items: 2 tbsp water (or water from boiling the dumplings)
2 tbsp Chinese black vinegar (or substitute rice vinegar)

steps: Heat oil until almost smoking. In a heatsafe bowl, add garlic, cilantro, green onions, chilli and sesame seeds and pour over oil to get aromatics to “sizzle.”
Add remainder of ingredients. Use as dipping sauce or drizzle on dumplings. Any ingredient can included or omitted.

items: ¼-½ cup pine nuts, toasted (use as much as desired)
1 large handful of basil, cut in a chiffonade

steps: Preheat oven to 400 F.. Carefully score the eggplant flesh without cutting into skin. Rub 2 tsp salt into flesh and set aside for 5-10 minutes, then rinse and pat dry. Combine cumin with 2 tbs olive oil and brush over flesh. Heat a large frypan over medium heat and cook eggplant, flesh-side down, for 10-15 minutes until dark golden. Transfer eggplant, flesh-side up, to a baking tray lined with baking paper. Bake for 30-40 minutes until a skewer easily pierces flesh. Cool slightly.

Using a spoon, scoop out eggplant flesh, leaving 1cm attached and reserving skin. Combine eggplant mixture with pine nuts, garlic, basil leaves, sumac, half the cheese and remaining 1 tbs oil. Spoon into eggplant skin and top with remaining cheese. Bake for 15 minutes or until golden. Scatter with extra pine nuts and basil leaves to serve.

items: 1 hot pepper, diced (jalapeno or serrano are fine)

steps: Brown the ground beef: Heat a large 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Add the ground beef, season with salt and pepper, and brown, breaking into smaller pieces with a spatula or spoon. When browned, place onto a paper towel lined plate, and drain the beef. Set aside. (You can add ½ tsp of dry mustard to beef as it cooks as well.)

Cook the pepper, mushrooms and onion: In the same pan, add in the bell pepper and onion. After vegetables soften, add mushroom slices. Cook until all is golden brown and softened and mushrooms have released their liquid. Add the garlic and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Season with salt and pepper. Transfer this mixture to another plate and set aside.

Make the sauce: In a saucepan, add butter and melt. Add flour and cook 1-2 minutes, until flour is golden. Add half-and-half and whisk until the sauce thickens. Add stock and whisk until the sauce thickens.
Cook the noodles: Add the egg noodles and cook according to instructions.

Assemble and broil casserole: Turn oven onto broiler setting. In a casserole dish, add the ground beef, green peppers, mushrooms, and onions, egg noodles, and sauce. Stir to combine. Lastly, stir in the shredded cheese, or simply put cheese on top of casserole. Place under broiler and broiler 2-3 minutes until cheese is brown and bubbly. Watch carefully as it broils so that it doesn’t overcook. Serve immediately.

items: 2 tbsp gluten free oat flour (or gluten free flour blend, chickpea flour, or even white flour)
1½ tsp sea salt, plus more to taste
Both optional: Pinch cayenne pepper and a pinch ground cardamom
Safflower or grapeseed (or other high smoke point) oil for pan frying

steps:
Rinse (uncooked) chickpeas in a fine mesh strainer and add to a large pot. Cover with 2 inches water and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil for 1 minute, then cover, remove from heat, and let set for 1 hour. Then drain and lightly rinse and dry thoroughly (method from [the Kitchn](http://www.thekitchn.com/how-to-quicksoak-dried-beans-cooking-lessons-from-the-kitchn-198610)).
In the meantime, add parsley, onion and garlic to a food processor. Mix until well processed.

Once the chickpeas are slightly cooled and dried, add to the food processor that has the parsley and onion mixture, along with gluten free oat flour, salt, cumin, cardamom, coriander, and cayenne (optional). Mix to combine thoroughly, scraping down sides as needed. This may take up to 4-5 minutes to fully incorporate all of the spices and herbs. You're looking for a near paste with only very small bits of chickpeas and herbs.
Sample a small bit and adjust spices/salt/herbs as needed. Then cover and set in the refrigerator for 1 hour to allow the flavors to meld and the texture to become more firm.

Once cooled, remove from refrigerator and scoop out approximately 1½ tbs amounts and gently form into small discs using your hands. If the falafel isn't sticking together the mixture may need to be blended more thoroughly, or dusted with a bit more flour if too wet.

Once your falafels are formed (~24 total), heat a large metal or cast iron skillet over medium/ medium-high heat. Once hot, add enough oil to create a thin layer on the bottom of the pan and wait 1-2 minutes for the oil to heat up. Then place only as many falafel as will fit comfortably in the pan and cook 2-3 minutes on each side or until brown on each side. Once the bottom side is browned, flip gently as they can be fragile. Continue until all falafel are cooked.

Adjust heat as needed if they're browning too quickly, or aren't cooking quickly enough.
These falafel are delicious on their own with hummus or a tahini sauce. I also love garnishing them with chili garlic sauce for heat (such as sambal oelek.) Serve over greens or in pita.
To freeze, pan-fry falafel, let cool, then add to a freezer safe container and freeze up to 1 month. Reheat in a 375 degree F (190 C) oven until warmed through.

sections.name: Easy Tahini Sauce

items: Za’atar, to taste but about 1 tbs (optional)
Cumin, to taste but about 1 tsp (optional)

steps: Mix all ingredients together. Taste for seasoning and adjust. If sauce is too thick, add water 1 tsp at a time until desired consistency is achieved.

items: 1 lb. flounder fillet (also called fluke), divided depending on size, usually ⅓ to ½ lb of fish per person is good
Ciabatta bread or rolls, sliced lengthwise
Salad greens/spinach, herbs such as cilantro, dill, or mint, or a mix of any of this

steps: Combine the mayonnaise and sriracha. Stir well and set aside.
In a separate bowl, whisk together the vinegar, sugar, and salt. Add the red onions and let hang out for 20 minutes or so.
In a third bowl, add the fish sauce and the flounder. Toss well, cover with plastic and let hang out in the fridge for 20 minutes. Dry on paper towels.

Place a large skillet set over high heat. When hot, pour in a tablespoon of canola oil and then add the flounder, one piece at a time if pan would be crowded with all of the pieces. Sear on both sides. Repeat if necessary with the rest of the fillets.
Toast the bread/rolls if desired. Then smear the sriracha mayonnaise on the insides of the cut bread. Add the fish, herbs and/or greens, and pickled onions between the bread. Serve.

items: 2 tablespoons (1/4 stick) butter or olive oil
Half a large onion or 1 small onion, chopped
8-10 garlic cloves, peeled (original recipe calls for 18, but that is too strong for us!)
3 1/2 cups chicken stock or canned low-salt chicken broth

steps: Preheat oven to 350°F. Place 26 garlic cloves in small glass baking dish. Add 2 tablespoons olive oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper; toss to coat. Cover baking dish tightly with foil and bake until garlic is golden brown and tender, about 45 minutes. Cool. Squeeze garlic between fingertips to release cloves. Transfer cloves to small bowl.

Melt butter in heavy large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add onions and thyme and cook until onions are translucent, about 6 minutes. Add roasted garlic and raw garlic cloves and cook 3 minutes. Add chicken stock; cover and simmer until garlic is very tender, about 20 minutes. Working in batches, puree soup in blender until smooth. Return soup to saucepan and bring to simmer. Season with salt and pepper.
Divide grated cheese as desired among bowls and ladle soup over. We usually use about 2 teaspoons to a tablespoon of cheese per bowl. Squeeze juice of a lemon wedge into each bowl and serve.

items: 4 cups of broth, vegetable or chicken
1 sprig each of thyme, oregano, or rosemary, as available or desired
1 cup pastina, alphabet pasta, or desired pasta shape
½ cup of pecorino or parmigiano reggiano
1 cup of chopped fresh spinach or kale (optional)

steps: Heat olive oil over medium-low heat in soup pot or dutch oven. If using onion, carrots, or celery, saute until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic to pot and saute for 1 minute. Salt vegetables.
Add broth and herbs to pot. Adjust heat to medium to bring to simmer and then simmer on low heat for 15 minutes.

Add peas and greens, if using and cook another couple of minutes until soup is at a strong simmer again. Add pasta and simmer until pasta is cooked. Stir in cheese off heat and then serve with black pepper.

ingredient_groups.name: Sauce
items: 1 Tbsp rice vinegar (or black chinese/Chinkiang vinegar)
1/4 cup coconut sugar, maple syrup, or honey, plus more to taste
3 Tbsp tamari or soy sauce (or 2 Tbsp regular soy sauce and 1 Tbsp dark soy sauce)
1 Tbsp Sambal Oelek, Siracha, or other hot sauce
1 tsp roasted and ground Sichuan peppercorns (optional)
1 Tbsp Shaoxing wine, rice wine, sherry, sake, brandy, or white wine

ingredient_groups.name: Tofu
items: 3 Tbsp tamari or soy sauce (tamari for gluten free eaters)
2 Tbsp neutral oil (such as grape seed or canola)

ingredient_groups.name: Stir Fry
items: 1 bundle green onions, bulbs removed, roughly chopped
4-7 dried red chilies (optional for heat, or sub 1 Tbsp chili garlic sauce)

steps: Place all tofu ingredients besides tofu and cornstarch in bowl and mix to combine. Chop tofu into pieces and then place in zip lock bag with sauce. Shake contents to cover tofu and then begin adding cornstarch, 1 tablespoon at a time, until cornstarch and sauce form a coating that covers the tofu.
Fry tofu in oil in a cast iron pan over medium heat, flipping to fry all sides until crispy. When you take tofu out of bag, let excess sauce pour off, before placing in hot pan.
Reserve fried tofu as needed. In a clean pan, saute fried tofu, scallions, and chilis, and then while on heat toss in sauce and serve.

title: Greek Lamb Stew/Pasta Sauce with Orzo

items: 1 lb. boneless lamb shoulder or leg, trimmed of excess fat and cut in small 1-inch pieces
1 28 oz. can whole San Marzano tomatoes, with juice

steps: Pat meat dry using paper towels, then season generously using salt and pepper. Heat olive oil over medium-high heat in a large Dutch oven. Add meat and sear until browned on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes total. Transfer browned meat to a plate using a slotted spoon.
Turn heat to medium. Toss onions into pot, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom, and cook until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 more minute until fragrant.

Return meat and any juices to Dutch oven. Pour in wine, scraping up frond, and simmer until reduced by half. Add oregano, paprika, cinnamon, nutmeg, and bay leaf. Add tomatoes with juices, crushing them slightly with wooden spoon.
Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and gently simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour, until meat is tender.
Stir in orzo pasta directly into stew. Add a splash of water or broth if liquid level is too low. Simmer uncovered, stirring occasionally, about 15 minutes until orzo is tender and sauce is absorbed.
Remove from heat and let sit 5 to 10 minutes. Garnish with fresh parsley and feta cheese before serving.

sections.name: Alternative
steps: Substitute ground lamb, reduce simmering time to 10 minutes, cook orzo separately, and serve as a pasta sauce.

items: 8 large chicken thighs, overlapping skin trimmed
5 medium Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled, cut into large chunks, and soaked in water then dried

steps: Add garlic, olive oil, lemon juice, Dijon mustard, honey, dried oregano, dried thyme, sea salt, and black pepper to a blender and blend until smooth. Place chicken thighs in a sealable bag or large bowl, pour the marinade over, and mix to coat thoroughly. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Preheat oven to 425°F with the rack set to the middle level. Arrange the dried potato chunks in a single layer in a baking dish and pour half of the used marinade over them, using your hands to coat them thoroughly.
Place the chicken thighs on top of the potatoes, skin side up, and drizzle the remaining marinade over the chicken.

Bake for 10 minutes, then reduce the oven temperature to 375°F. Continue baking for 45 to 55 minutes, or until the chicken reaches an internal temperature of 185°F. If the potatoes need more time to become tender and brown, transfer the chicken to a plate, tent with foil, raise the oven temperature back to 425°F, and roast the potatoes for a few extra minutes.
Let the dish sit lightly tented with foil for 10 to 15 minutes before serving to reabsorb the pan juices. Garnish with fresh oregano and lemon slices if desired.

title: Greek Salad with Broccoli and Sun-Dried Tomatoes

items: Mixed greens, with or without herbs
1 small head broccoli florets, broken into florets
Small handful sunflower seeds or pepitas

steps: Heat a cast-iron pan on medium-hot until very hot. Put in broccoli florets, florets facing down, in pan without any oil. Brown the florets all over without oil. The pan may smoke while you char the broccoli.
Toss everything besides the broccoli and chickpeas together.

After the broccoli is charred as much as you want, remove and put with other salad ingredients. Turn off for several minutes to allow the pan to cool and then turn the heat to medium. Add olive oil and chickpeas and fry until crispy, about 5 to 8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Toss chickpeas with salad and dress salad with vinaigrette of choice (I like a simple dressing of olive oil and lemon juice or sherry vinegar.)

items: 8 tablespoons (4 ounces/1 stick) unsalted butter, cut into several pieces
1 1/2 cup (6 ounces) grated cheese, like gruyère or cheddar

steps: Boil the Water and Butter: Combine the water, butter, salt, and mustard (if using) in a 2- to 4-quart saucepan and bring to a rolling boil.
Add the Flour: Once all the butter has melted, remove the pan from heat and add the flour all at once. Stir vigorously until the mixture comes together and resembles mashed potatoes.

Cook the Dough: Return the pan to medium-low heat and stir for 3-5 minutes to dry out the dough. The dough is ready when it glistens and is thick enough to hold a spoon upright. Some starch buildup on the bottom of the pan is normal.

Add the Eggs: Transfer the dough to the bowl of a stand mixer fitted with a paddle attachment. (The following steps can also be done with a hand mixer or by hand with a stiff spatula.) Beat the dough on a medium-low speed for one minute until it stops steaming and is just warm to the touch. Continue beating and add the egg in four additions. Wait for each addition to be absorbed and for the dough to smooth out before adding the next. Scrape down the sides of the bowl if needed between additions. In the end, the dough should come together in a very smooth, creamy batter. Beat in the cheese.

Bake the Gougères: Heat the oven to 450°F. Scoop rounded tablespoons of dough onto sheet pans lined with silicone mats or parchment paper. Space them at least an inch apart. Bake the gougères for 5 minutes and then turn the heat down to 350°F. Bake for another 20-25 minutes, rotating the pans once during baking. The finished gougères will be puffed, deep golden-brown, and dry to the touch (the cheese may still be bubbling a bit). They will also feel light and hollow when picked up.

Cool the Gougères: Transfer the sheet pan to a cooling rack. Serve warm or room temperature. Leftovers can be stored in the refrigerator and re-crisped in a warm oven before serving or frozen for up to three months.

items: 1 lb (450g) very thinly sliced pork, any cut
2 tablespoon Korean chili flakes or 1 teaspoon or other chili powder
1 teaspoon fresh ginger finely minced or 1/2 teaspoon ginger powder
1 tablespoon corn syrup or mirin, optional

steps: In a small mixing bowl combine chili paste, chili flakes/powder, soy sauces, sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil, sesame seeds, and corn syrup, mix well.
In a large mixing bowl combine pork with the sauce, and mix well to coat all the pork slices with the sauce evenly.

Drizzle 1 Tbsp oil to the skillet and bring it over medium-high heat. Place pork over the skillet and add the sliced onion on top. When they sizzle, start tossing everything to cook evenly all the way or until the pork is fully cooked and onions are soft, about 3-5 minutes.

items: 4-5 orange habanero peppers, deseeded to taste
1 very small or ½ of a small onion, chopped

steps: Cook unpeeled garlic in a saucepan on high heat, until browned and softened, 10-15 minutes. Take out of pan and peel when cool.
Add vinegar, carrot, onion, and peppers to saucepan and cook on medium heat until carrot is softened, about 10 minutes. Add garlic cloves when they are peeled to vinegar mixture.
Purée vinegar mixture in blender or food processor with sugar and salt. Add water to achieve desired consistency.

items: 3 ounces (about 1 ⅓ cups) finely grated Gruyère or Comté cheese
2 ounces (about ⅔ cups) finely grated Parmigiano-Reggiano
1 tablespoon fresh thyme leaves, roughly chopped Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
4 to 4 ½ pounds russet potatoes (about 7 to 8 medium), peeled and sliced ⅛-inch thick on a mandoline slicer

steps: Adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 400°F (200°C). Grease a 2-quart casserole dish (or 9x13-inch baking dish) with the softened butter.
Combine the grated Gruyère and Parmigiano-Reggiano in a large bowl. Transfer ⅓ of the cheese mixture to a separate bowl and set aside for the final topping.
Add the heavy cream, minced garlic, and chopped thyme to the large bowl with the remaining cheese. Season generously with kosher salt and black pepper.

Add the sliced potatoes to the bowl and toss with your hands until every slice is coated with the cream mixture, making sure to separate any slices that are sticking together so the liquid gets in between them.

Pick up a handful of potatoes, organize them into a neat stack, and lay them in the prepared casserole dish with their edges aligned vertically. Continue placing potatoes in the dish, working around the perimeter and into the center until all the potatoes are added and tightly packed. If necessary, slice an additional potato, coat it with the cream mixture, and add it to the dish.
Pour any excess cream and cheese mixture evenly over the potatoes until it comes about halfway up the sides of the dish.
Cover the dish tightly with aluminum foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Remove the foil and continue baking until the top is pale golden brown, about 30 minutes longer.
Carefully remove from the oven, sprinkle the reserved ⅓ of the cheese mixture evenly over the top, and return to the oven.
Bake until deep golden brown and crisp on top, about 20 to 30 minutes longer. Remove from the oven, let rest for a few minutes, and serve.

sources.text: J. Kenji López-Alt via Serious Eats / J. Kenji López-Alt on Food Lab

items: 2 cloves garlic, grated on a microplane (about 2 teaspoons)
1 tablespoons crushed red pepper flakes (hot sausage only)
Dash of ground cayenne pepper (hot sausage only)

steps: Thoroughly mix everything together in a mixing bowl until pork starts to emulsify.

items: 1 scotch bonnet/habanero, deseeded and minced or kept whole to be less spicy
Additional chopped green scallions for serving

steps: Season oxtails with jerk seasoning if using and otherwise with salt and pepper and brown in neutral oil in dutch oven.
Reserve oxtails and saute all vegetables except garlic, ginger, and hot pepper. Once the onion has softened, add garlic, ginger, and hot pepper, saute 1 minute and then add tomato paste.

Once tomato paste and all vegetables are aromatic, add in broth and then the rest of the seasonings. Once mixed, add in oxtails and braise for 2 to 3 hours or until tender, adding more broth if the liquid evaporates or is too thick. Traditionally butter beans are added but I have never done so and serve it over coconut rice and sauteed greens, preferably collared greens or callaloo (which is very hard to source outside of Jamaica and the Cayman Islands.)

items: ¼ cup safflower or other neutral oil
1-2 scotch bonnets/habanero, seeded and chopped (2 will definitely be hotter)
3-4 lbs skin-on chicken thighs, boned or boneless (with bones just take longer to bake), with skin trimmed

steps: Wash and thoroughly pat dry chicken thighs. Salt both sides of thighs and and put in fridge for several hours.
Put together all ingredients other than the chicken in a mini-chop, food processor, or blender and puree.

2-4 hours before baking, put chicken thighs in a bowl and cover in marinade. Make sure to thoroughly cover each chicken thigh with marinade, massaging it in. Use gloves or thoroughly wash your hands before and after, because the habanero can cause an uncomfortable chili burn.

Pre-heat oven to 350. Put a wire rack in a rimmed baking sheet and evenly place chicken thighs on rack (you can do it with the wire rack, but the chicken won’t be as crispy.) Bake until chicken thighs read 155-160 degrees fahrenheit with an instant read thermometer. If you have leftover marinade, I baste the chicken thighs with it every 10 or 15 minutes. Then, put move chicken to broiler and broil 3-5 minutes until skin is crispy and charred. Serve with rice and greens. Anything with pineapple (or just pineapple) would also make a great side.

items: 1 cup finely chopped kimchi, plus ⅓ cup kimchi juice
1 pound/package fresh or frozen udon noodles
3-6 scallions, white and pale-green parts only, thinly sliced on a diagonal, to taste
1 package thinly-sliced berkshire pork as found in Japanese and Korean markets

steps: Heat 2 Tbsp. butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Add chopped kimchi and gochujang and cook, stirring occasionally, until kimchi is softened and lightly caramelized, about 4 minutes. Add pork if using and cook until slightly browned, about another 4 minutes. Add garlic and saute another minute. Add broth and kimchi juice and bring to a simmer. Cook until liquid is slightly reduced, about 3 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil noodles according to package directions.

Using tongs, transfer noodles to skillet and add remaining 3 Tbsp. butter; cook, tossing often, until sauce coats noodles, about 2 minutes. Season with salt if needed. Divide among bowls and top with egg yolks, scallions, and sesame seeds.

items: ½ cup cabbage kimchi, roughly chopped
½ cup kimchi juice (or less depending on how much is in the jar), water may be substituted
2-3 tablespoons water, depending on desired consistency of batter

steps: In a large bowl, combine the flour, rice flour, pepper, garlic powder, and salt until combined. Add the kimchi, kimchi juice, water, and scallions. Use a pair of chopsticks or a fork to stir the mixture until well-combined.

Heat a nonstick or cast iron pan over medium high heat. Add 2 tablespoons vegetable oil and add the batter to the pan, spreading it in an even layer. Fry until browned on one side. Flip the pancake and continue to cook until browned on the other side. Alternatively, fry smaller round pancakes approximately two inches wide, again flipping halfway through. Rest fried pancake on a paper towel several minutes before eating.
Meanwhile, assemble the dipping sauce by combining the sauce ingredients in a small bowl. Serve alongside the pancake!

sections.name: Dipping Sauce
steps: Stir all of the ingredients together.

items: ½ cup of olive oil or other flavor-less oil, or mixture of both (I prefer a 50/50 mixture)
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
3/4 cup of grated pecorino or parmigiano
1 small white onion or 2 shallots, finely sliced (optional)

steps: Break down kale from thick stalks and chop to manageable size, wash, and reserve.

First, make a fresh mayonnaise. Whisk the egg in small bowl, until yolk is emulsified with whites. Add some salt and whisk some more (salt further breaks up the egg.) Then slowly pour in oil in a steady stream while continuing to whisk, until an emulsion forms. If you add the oil too fast, the emulsion will break and require you to whisk an egg yolk into the mixture to reform the emulsion. Keep on adding oil, until you have about ½ or ⅔ of a cup (depending on how much kale you have) of the mayonnaise.

Add anchovies, garlic, most of the cheese (can reserve 1 or 2 tablespoons), Worcestershire, lemon juice, mustard, and onion (if using). Whisk until dressing has ingredients evenly incorporated. Add lots of freshly cracked pepper.
Coat kale with reserved cheese (this helps the dressing adhere to the kale.) Toss with dressing and serve.

notes.name: Optional protein addition
notes.text: Drain 1 can of chickpeas and rinse thoroughly. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil over medium-high heat in a cast iron pan and add chickpeas. Saute/fry until chickpeas are nice and brown, approximately 8-10 minutes. Serve chickpeas on top of kale salad.

items: 8 oz button mushrooms, cleaned and sliced
½ cup white wine, chicken stock, or water
1 bunch kale, ribs removed and chopped
1-2 cups of chicken stock (as needed per farro’s cooking directions)

steps: Start cooking farro per instructions, substituting stock for water.
If using, fry the bacon until slightly crisp. Drain on a paper towel. Reserve bacon grease for another use (roasting potatoes, cooking greens, etc.)

Add the butter to a skillet. Add the onions and cook them over medium-low heat for 10 to 15 minutes, until soft. Remove them to a plate. Add the mushrooms, stir, then add the wine, and season with salt and pepper. Turn the heat to medium-high and cook the mushrooms for several minutes, until most of the wine has evaporated and the mushrooms are soft. Remove them from the heat and set them aside.
Whisk the olive oil, vinegar, thyme, salt, and pepper to form a vinaigrette.

Toss kale in a large bowl with half the dressing. Then add mushrooms, onions, and bacon and toss again. Finally, add the goat cheese and more dressing if needed, and toss. (Reserve extra dressing for another use.)
Serve kale and mushroom salad over the farro.

title: Kale, Poblano, and Black Bean Tacos

items: 1 bunch of kale (any type), peeled off stalks and chopped
1 14 oz can of black beans, drained and rinsed
1 Tbs chili powder (mixture of different chiles is best, including ancho, chipotle, hatch, etc.)
Some chorizo sausage, out of casings (optional)
Soft tacos for serving and any taco fixings you like

steps: If using sausage, brown in olive oil over medium heat, using back of wooden spoon to break up into small pieces. Otherwise, saute onion and peppers over medium heat.
Once onions are translucent and peppers are soft, add garlic and kale and ¼ cup of water. Cover if possible and saute/steam kale until tender.

Add black beans, chili powder, salt and pepper, and sausage if using to kale mixture. Saute until beans are cooked through and flavors are incorporated. Add water 1 Tbs at time if mixture is too dry and burning. Serve in soft tacos with hot sauce, avocados, cheese of choice, radishes, etc.

items: 1 Tbs, gochujang (or doubanjiang [fermented chili broad bean paste])
1 Tsp, Better than Bouillon beef stock seasoning
2 Tbs rice wine, dry sherry, white wine, or beer
1 Tbs brown sugar (optional, or add 1 Tbs of mirin)
1 bunch baby bok choy, cleaned and chopped into 1-2” pieces
1 package dried shiitake mushrooms, soaked in warm water for 30 minutes

steps: Cut brisket into 1 inch cubes and season liberally with salt (~1-2 teaspoons). In pressure cooker, put on saute function and add onion. Saute until soft and golden, approximately 5-10 minutes. Add garlic and ginger and stir for 1 minute. Add brisket cubes and seasonings - the gochujang, soy sauce, Better than Bouillon beef stock, hondashi, cinnamon, star anise, wine, rice vinegar, sugar. Add 8 cups of water or stock. If using beef stock, omit the Better than Bouillon beef stock.

Seal cooker and cook for 45 minutes at 12.0 PSI. Allow for natural pressure release for 20 minutes and then manually release the rest of the pressure. Set to simmer/reduce function and add bok choy and mushrooms and cook for 7-8 minutes or until bok choy is completely wilted.
Serve with noodles, if desired. I like to add chinese [chili oil](recipe:chili-oil) (specifically [chili oil](recipe:chili-oil) with fermented black beans) to up the heat and funk.

ingredient_groups.name: Yogurt Pie Crust
items: 3 1/2 cups whole spelt flour or wheat flour

ingredient_groups.name: Pie Filling
items: 1 Tablespoon cooking fat (butter, ghee, lard, oil)
1-2 medium sized beets cut into 1/4 inch chunks (about 1 1/2 cups worth of chopped beets)
3 cups low salt broth (beef, lamb, pork, chicken or even veggie)

steps: The night before you plan on making your pot pie, prepare the dough. Cream together the yogurt and butter. Blend in the flour and salt. Cover with a dish towel and leave in a warm spot in your kitchen for 12-24 hours.

Prepare the pie filling by browning the lamb in a large cast iron pan over medium-high heat until cooked through and no longer pink. Use a slotted spoon to remove the lamb to a plate and keep to the side. Add the cooking fat to the pan and once melted add the onion, spices and salt. Cook, stirring occasionally for about 5 minutes. Add the tomato paste and beets and continue to cook, stirring often for about 2 minutes longer. Sprinkle in the flour and stir well. Add the red wine and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook until the wine reduces by about half. Slowly pour in the stock. Bring to a boil. Reduce the heat and simmer until the beets become tender and the mixture thickens up a bit, 8-10 minutes. Return the lamb to the pot along with the parsley and give it good stir. Remove from the heat.
Preheat the oven to 350F.

In a small bowl make an egg wash by whisking together the egg with the milk or cream. Then on a generously floured work surface, work the dough into a ball (if not already) and divide in half. Cover one half with beeswax wrap or plastic wrap and store in your fridge for later (up to 5 days) roll the remainder dough out with a well floured rolling pin into approximately 1/8 inch thick round (the dough is a bit stickier than your average dough but you'll get the hang of working with it!) Place the dough over the pot and fold the overhand inward while pinching to crimp the edges. Cut vents in the dough and brush with the egg wash.
Place pie on a rimmed baking sheet and bake until the crust is golden brown and the filling is bubbling around the edges, about 50-55 minutes. Cool for 10 minutes before serving

items: Fresh Cilantro and sliced radishes, to top soup

steps: Warm olive oil in a dutch oven and saute garlic and shallots for 3 minutes until soft. Add lentils, coconut oil, ginger, fennel seeds, and tumeric. Allow coconut oil to melt and softly saute spices. Then add the rest of the ingredients and 5 cups of water. Bring to a simmer and cook 40 minutes. Add more water if mixture is too thick.
Serve with cilantro and sliced radishes on top. You can also serve this with sprouts or over rice or with flatbread.

items: 1 1/2 cups dry red (preferably but any lentils will work) lentils, rinsed
½ Tsp garam masala or curry powder
6 cups loosely packed shredded greens, like beet greens, spinach, kale, or swiss chard
1 clove garlic, smashed, but left whole

steps: Place the lentils in a pot and add 4 cups of water to cover them. Most recipes say to use a 3 to 1 ratio of water to lentils, but because the lentils will be added to a watery sauce to finish cooking, use a little bit less here. Bring the water to a boil, skimming off any scum that rises to the top, then turn down the heat and simmer for 20 minutes, or until creamy and tender.

While the lentils are cooking, heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a heavy-based pan over medium-high heat. Add the onion and fry gently for about 5 minutes, until translucent and beginning to brown. Add the tomatoes and ginger, and cook for 3 minutes, until tomatoes soften. Add the turmeric and stir. Stir in the greens and let them wilt, time depends on the green.

Stir in the onion-tomato-greens into the lentils or vice versa depending on which pot can better fit the dal, and simmer for a few minutes to warm through, the flavors meld, and everything is fully cooked-through. Add more water if the lentils need some to finish cooking. Season to taste with the salt.

In a small pan, heat the remaining 1 tablespoon of oil, and add the cumin seeds and garlic clove. Fry for 30 seconds, until the cumin sizzles, then turn off the heat and pour the seasoned oil, cumin seeds and garlic into the dal. Cover and let it infuse.
Stir before serving, and serve hot with Naan or roti or other indian bread and a salad on the side.

Saute the carrots, celery, onion, and fennel in a dutch oven or other soup pot for 8 to 10 minutes until the onion is translucent and the vegetables are soft. Add the garlic and tomato paste and stir for 30 seconds. Add the diced tomato and saute for another 2 minutes.
Add the lentils, broth, zest, and fresh herbs. Bring to a boil, then simmer until lentils are at desired doneness, typically 40 or 50 minutes.

When lentils are done, take two ladleful of the vegetables (try to leave some of the broth in each scoop in the soup pot) and add to a blender. Blend until completely pureed. Add the puree back to the soup pot and stir. The soup may be too thick. If necessary, add more water by measuring water in bowl of blender to help get any remaining bits of puree. When at desired consistency, bring to simmer, season with salt and pepper, and serve.

items: 2 Tbsp (30 ml) grape seed or coconut oil
1 white or yellow onion, diced (110 g)
1/2 tsp each sea salt and black pepper, divided (plus more to taste)
2 15-ounce or 1 28-ounce (425 g) can(s) diced tomatoes, unsalted, or whole-peeled tomatoes
1 3/4 cup (420 ml) water, plus more as needed
3/4 cup (148g) dry red lentils, thoroughly rinsed in cold water + drained
1 15-ounce (425 g) can kidney beans, slightly drained
1 15-ounce (425 g) can black beans, slightly drained
1-2 Tbsp (12-24 g) coconut sugar (or maple syrup)

steps: Heat a large pot over medium heat. Once hot, add oil, onion, and red pepper. Season with a healthy pinch each salt and pepper and stir. Sauté for 3-4 minutes, stirring frequently. Add jalapeño and garlic and saute 1 minute more.

Add 2 Tbsp chili powder, 1 Tbsp cumin, paprika, diced tomatoes, tomato paste, and water, and stir to combine. Bring to a low boil over medium high heat. If using whole-peeled tomatoes, crush with your hands in the pot.

Once boiling, add lentils and reduce heat to medium-low or low, so it's at a gentle simmer. You want to see bubbles, but you don't want it boiling. Cook for 15 minutes, or until lentils are mostly tender. As it's cooking you may need to add more water if the mixture is looking too dry and the lentils aren't submerged (I didn't find that necessary).
Next add kidney beans, black beans, 1/4 tsp each salt and pepper, and remaining 1 Tbsp cumin, and 1 Tbsp chili powder, and stir to combine.
Bring to a simmer over medium heat, then reduce heat slightly to low (or medium-low), add corn (optional), cover, and gently simmer for 20 minutes to meld the flavors together. Stir occasionally.

Taste and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more chili powder or cumin for smokiness, salt for saltiness, or a little coconut sugar to balance the heat and draw out the other flavors. Serve as is, or garnished with chili cheese fritos, fresh jalapeño, cilantro, red onion, and/or avocado (optional).

items: 1 6 oz package of button mushrooms, minced
3-4 scallions, white and dark green parts separated and chopped
1-2 dried chile de arbol (whole) or fresh thai chilies (thinly sliced)
2 tablespoons Shaoxing or Chinese cooking wine
1 tablespoon fermented chili broad bean paste
2 tablespoons Sichuan peppercorns, 1 tablespoon left whole, the other toasted and ground in a spice grinder or mortar and pestle
1 pound silken tofu, diced into large pieces

steps: In a wok or large pot such as a dutch oven, gently fry the mushrooms in the oil, reserving 1 tablespoon, for 5-10 minutes until all of the water is released and they have fried to desired texture. Remove from pan.

Add last tablespoon of oil into pan/pot, and saute ginger, garlic, white scallion parts, and chilis for 1 minute. Add in chinese wine and cook off and then add in chili bean paste and sichuan peppercorns and coat the aromatics in the paste, frying for another minute.
Take a tablespoon or two of broth and mix in corn starch. Add in soy sauces and chicken broth to pan/pot and warm up. Once the sauce is simmering, add in mushrooms and then corn starch mixture.
On a gentle simmer, gently add in tofu and cook through. Serve with rice, green scallions.

items: 1 ½ - 2 cups of heavy cream and/or milk (1 cup of each is best)
8 ounces mixed rindless soft and semi-soft cheeses (such as Gruyere, Fontina, Cheddar, Gorgonzola, Stilton, Jack, etc.), cubed or broken into small clumps
4 sage leaves or other herbs for decoration (optional)
1 pre-made pie crust in pie dish, defrosted, or buttered 9” casserole for crustless quiche

steps: Preheat oven to 425F and set rack to center position. Line the dough with parchment paper, allowing it to overhang the sides, and fill the pan with pie weights, dried beans, or dry rice. Bake the crust for 10 minutes. Remove weights and parchment paper, wrap edges of the pie dough with tin foil, and return to the oven. Bake until lightly golden brown, 3 to 5 minutes. Remove and lower oven temperature to 350F. If not using crust, skip this step and just preheat oven to 350F.
In a large bowl, whisk cream and milk with eggs until thoroughly incorporated. Whisk salt and pepper into custard base.

Scatter half of cheese and vegetable filling all over bottom of pie and set on a rimmed baking sheet. Pour in half of custard mixture or until first layer of fillings and cheese is covered. Add second half of cheese and vegetable filling and pour remaining custard on top. Arrange decorative herbs on top of custard.

Bake until center is just barely set but still jiggles when touched, about 35 minutes. Remove from oven and allow to cool at least 15 minutes before serving. Serve warm, sprinkling minced chives on top, if desired.

notes.name: Note
notes.text: various vegetable filling ideas include (1) mushrooms/shallots or mushrooms/leeks with blue cheese; (2) spinach and leek with feta, (3) bacon/scallions/onions with gruyere or cheddar; (4) asparagus/shallot with fontina or gruyere (5) mushrooms/onions and swiss; (6) smoked salmon/red onion with swiss or gruyere.

notes.name: Note
notes.text: all vegetables or bacon should be fully cooked/sauteed before adding to quiche. Spinach and mushrooms need all of the water cooked out, otherwise they will destroy the consistency of your custard.

title: Miso Soup with Mushrooms and Escarole

items: 1 Head Escarole, cut into bite size pieces

steps: Heat olive oil over medium-low heat. Add leek and saute until soft, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and chile and saute another minute.

Add stock and miso paste and bring to a simmer. Make sure miso paste is fully dissolved, then add mushrooms and escarole. Simmer until vegetables are soft. Serve with a poached or fried egg on top or without for a vegan meal. Season with salt and pepper.

items: 1 cup soup pasta or broken spaghetti

steps: Bring chicken stock/broth, juiced lemons, and bay leaf to a simmer. Add onion, celery, and carrots and cook until tender.
Add pasta and cook until al dente. Add chicken and heat through. Finish by stirring in parsley and cheese.

items: 1½ to 1¾ pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts (or chicken tenderloins)
¼ cup extra virgin olive oil

steps: Pound out chicken breasts to even thickness, marinate 5-6 hours with the rest of the ingredients, and grill.

ingredient_groups.name: Eggplant & Potato Layer
items: 2 large Yukon Gold potatoes, peeled and sliced into 1/4-inch rounds

ingredient_groups.name: Meat Sauce
items: 1 1/2 pounds ground lamb (or a mix of lamb and beef)

ingredient_groups.name: Béchamel Sauce
items: 1/2 cup grated kefalotyri, pecorino, or parmesan cheese, plus extra for topping

steps: Salt eggplant slices and set aside in a colander for 30 minutes to draw out moisture. Rinse and pat thoroughly dry with paper towels.

Preheat oven to 400°F. Arrange eggplant and potato slices on oiled baking sheets, brush tops with olive oil, and season with salt. Roast until tender and lightly golden, about 20–25 minutes. Set aside and reduce oven temperature to 350°F.

Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant. Add ground lamb and cook, breaking up with a wooden spoon, until browned. Drain excess fat if needed.

Stir in tomato paste and cook 1 minute. Pour in red wine and simmer until mostly evaporated. Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, cinnamon, allspice, bay leaf, salt, and pepper. Simmer over low heat until thick, about 20 minutes. Remove bay leaf.

Meanwhile, melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in flour and cook, stirring constantly, for 1–2 minutes until smooth and pale golden. Slowly pour in warmed milk while whisking constantly to prevent lumps. Simmer gently, whisking often, until thickened enough to coat the back of a spoon, about 5–7 minutes.
Remove béchamel from heat and stir in nutmeg, salt, and grated cheese. Temper the beaten egg yolks with a splash of the warm sauce, then whisk them back into the saucepan until smooth.

Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Layer the roasted potatoes evenly on the bottom, followed by half of the eggplant slices. Spread the meat sauce evenly over the eggplant, then top with the remaining eggplant slices.
Pour the béchamel sauce over the top, smoothing it into an even layer, and sprinkle with extra grated cheese.
Bake at 350°F for 45–50 minutes until the top is puffed and deep golden brown. Let rest for 20–30 minutes before slicing and serving.

items: 2 pounds portobello mushrooms, in 1/4-inch slices (save the stems for another use) (you can use cremini instead, as well)
2 cups beef or vegetable broth (beef broth is traditional but vegetable to make it vegetarian; it works with either)
1 teaspoon fresh thyme leaves (1/2 teaspoon dried)
1 cup pearl onions, peeled (thawed if frozen)

steps: Heat the one tablespoon of the olive oil and one tablespoon of butter in a medium Dutch oven or heavy sauce pan over high heat. Sear the mushrooms until they begin to darken, but not yet release any liquid — about three or four minutes. Remove them from pan.

Lower the flame to medium and add the second tablespoon of olive oil. Toss the carrots, onions, leeks, thyme, a few good pinches of salt and a several grinds of black pepper into the pan and cook for 10, stirring occasionally, until the onions are lightly browned. Add the garlic, tomato paste, and flour and cook for just one or two more minutes.

Add the wine to the pot, scraping any stuck bits off the bottom, then turn the heat all the way up and reduce it by half and thickened. Stir in the broth, soy sauce, and marmite. Add back the mushrooms with any juices that have collected and once the liquid has boiled, reduce the temperature so it simmers for 20 minutes, or until mushrooms are very tender. Add the pearl onions and simmer for five minutes more.

items: 1/4 cup oyster sauce, or more to taste
1 tsp fish sauce, plus more for serving
1 bunch broccoli, florets cut into 1-inch pieces, stalks peeled and cut on bias into 1/2-inch pieces
1 bunch of bok choy, leaves and stems separated
1 package mushrooms, try to get shiitake (or boneless chicken breast, cut into chunks)
6 garlic cloves, sliced thin (depending on taste, but I always go heavy with the garlic)

steps: Mix first five ingredients together for sauce and set aside. Prepare rice noodles to stir fry according to package directions, typically you will have to run them over cold water to stop the cooking process, but you should do that regardless of what the package directions say.

Add 1 tbsp of oil to large cast iron skillet, heat over medium-high heat, and add in broccoli. Stir occasionally, but deeply char on as many sides as possible, about 10 minutes. Add in some water (stand back, because it will immediately steam) and cook until no water is left and broccoli is completely cooked through. Finish broccoli with 2 tbsp of sauce and mix to incorporate, set aside broccoli in a bowl, and place skillet back on medium-high heat.

Add 1 tbsp of oil and add in mushrooms (or chicken). Stir-fry until nicely browned and soft (or cooked through), about 5 to 7 minutes. Finish with garlic slices and 2 tbsp of sauce, cooking another 2 or 3 minutes. Set aside mushrooms (or chicken) and garlic to the bowl with broccoli.

Add 1 tbsp of oil and stir fry bok choy, first only with the stems. Once the stems have cooked 5 minutes, add leaves and 1 tbsp of sauce and stir fry until wilted. Move bok choy to edge of pan and add 1 tbsp of oil to open area of pan. Add eggs and stir fry until almost cooked through, breaking egg into smaller pieces. Set aside bok choy and egg mixture to the bowl with the other vegetables.

Add 1 tbsp of oil and add noodles. Stir fry for 2 minutes and then add 2 tbsp of sauce. Once noodles are evenly coated with sauce, add in rest of vegetables (and chicken), and any remaining sauce, and cook until everything is heat through.
Serve with cilantro and siracha.

items: ¾ lbs shrimp, tails on, bodies used for stock if available
Haricot vert/green beans, about 1 lb, trimmed and chopped into equal 1” pieces
5.5 - 6.25 cups of stock, best if mix of chicken and shrimp stock

steps: In paella pan over a stove at high heat, brown chicken, skin-side down, first, then flip and add chorizo and continue browning meat. Once thoroughly browned, add green beans and artichoke hearts. Top with rosemary sprigs. When vegetables are cooked softened, add salmorra as desired. Add saffron and then rice, and evenly distribute with meat and vegetables. Add stock to top of paella.
Top cooked paella with parsley and lemons.

sections.name: Salmorra

items: 2 dried ñora peppers, soaked 30 minutes in water or (red or white) wine and then minced with garlic

steps: Saute in ¼ of olive oil peppers and garlic for 1 minute. Then add tomatoes and cook until thickened, about 15 or 20 minutes. Deglaze with a little white wine or sherry and then add paprike and continue cooking until desired thickness.

items: 3 tablespoons melted butter or vegetable oil

steps: Whisk eggs into milk and stir in butter, vanilla (if using), and yeast (if using).
Whisk the dry ingredients together and then mix milk mixture with dry ingredients.
Let the batter rest for at least 15 minutes, while the griddle is heating; it'll thicken slightly. Let rest overnight on countertop if making yeasted pancakes
Cook 1/4 cupfuls of batter onto the lightly greased griddle. For blueberry pancakes, sprinkle the fresh or thawed frozen blueberries over the batter.

sources.text: J Kenji Alt-Lopez on Instagram for yeasted version.

title: Pasta with Braised Lamb Shank Ragu

items: 1 large or 2 medium onions trimmed and chopped
1 cup about 150 g oil cured black olives, pitted
Thin strips of peel from one orange (optional)
1/4 tsp Urfa pepper or a pinch of cayenne pepper or red pepper flakes

steps: Choose a stock pot, Dutch oven or braising dish that will hold the shanks and other ingredients so that the shanks can sit in one layer. Preheat oven to 325.

Pat the shanks dry with paper towel and season with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in the pot over medium heat and brown the shanks on all sides, about 10 minutes. When the shanks are browned, transfer them to a plate or platter.

Pour out the used oil from the pot and replace with more olive oil. Toss the carrots, celery, and onions into the pot. Season with salt (about 1 tsp) and cook over low heat, stirring until the vegetables are softened but not coloured, about 10 to 15 minutes.
Add in garlic and anchovies and saute while tossing for 1 to 2 minutes. Add in 1 ½ cup of white wine and deglaze. Reduce wine to ¾ cup of liquid.

we open the can of tomatoes and pour everything into a bowl. Using your hands to crush the tomatoes into bite sized chunks. Add the tomatoes and their juices, the olives and the citrus peel (if using) and the pepper into the pot. Stir everything to combine and bring up to a boil.

Add the lamb shanks to the pot. Ideally they should fit in one layer, and should be at least 3/4 submerged under the liquids. If not, add more white wine. Bring to a boil if lamb shanks or wine lowered the temperature of the liquid, place a lid on the pot, and then braise in oven. Check after half an hour to ensure there should be some bubbling going on. Adjust the heat to maintain this. Braise at least 2.5 hours and possible 3.5 hours until the lamb is tender and falling off the bone.
