Take braise out of oven and take out shanks and sprigs of herbs (and orange peel). Take meat off bone and shred and return to pot and bring to a slight simmer over stove if braise has cooled down. Serve over pasta of choice (fresh linguine is best) with chopped parsley.

items: 1 large head of broccoli (1¼–1½ pounds), cut into small florets and pieces
2 tablespoons extra-virgin olive oil, plus more for drizzling
½ cup of white wine or vermouth
½ cup of cream or half-and-half
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1/2 cup grated pecorino Romano, or more to taste.

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil and salt. Cook broccoli in salted boiling water until crisp-tender, about 3 minutes. Using a slotted spoon, transfer broccoli to a colander and let cool (save pot of water for cooking pasta).

Heat 2 Tbsp. oil in a large skillet over medium. Cook sausage and a generous pinch of red pepper flakes, breaking up meat into smaller pieces with a wooden spoon and stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through, 6–8 minutes.
Salt water, and cook pasta until tender but not mushy. Reserve about a cup of water before draining pasta.

While pasta is cooking, add garlic, shallot, sundried tomatoes, and blanched broccoli to pot with sausage, and cook for several minutes until fragrant. Break apart broccoli and sausage with the back of a wooden spoon or potato masher while everything cooks. Deglaze pan with white wine and simmer until wine is reduced. Add cream and cheese and incorporate, but do not cook cream for more than 1 minute before adding pasta.

When pasta is done, drain and toss sausage and broccoli sauce and add at least ½ cup of reserved pasta cooking water. Toss everything together as pasta finishes cooking. If the dressed pasta is dry, add a little reserved cooking water. Add plenty of black pepper and more cheese to taste, and serve.

items: 1/2 cup minced guanciale, pancetta or bacon (about 1/4 pound)
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 pound linguine or other long, thin pasta
1/2 cup grated pecorino Romano, or more to taste.

steps: Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. In a small saucepan, combine olive oil and meat, and turn heat to medium. Cook, stirring occasionally, until nicely browned, about 10 minutes. In the last minute, add the minced garlic (if using.) Turn off heat.
Salt water, and cook pasta until tender but not mushy. Reserve about a cup of water before draining pasta.
While pasta is cooking, beat 3 eggs in a large warmed bowl (large enough to hold pasta). Stir in about 1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan and the meat and its juices.

When pasta is done, drain and toss with egg mixture in the large bowl. NEVER make carbonara in a pot or pan that has been on heat as the egg will cook and not emulsify properly into a sauce. If the dressed pasta is dry, add a little reserved cooking water. Add plenty of black pepper and more Parmesan to taste, and serve.

items: 1 cup of dried chickpeas, soaked overnight
4 cloves garlic, 1 left whole and 3 sliced
Red pepper flakes, as much as desired

steps: Cover chickpeas in pot or pressure cooker with 2 or 3 inches of water. Add carrot, celery, half of onion, and 1 garlic clove. Salt water. Cook until slightly underdone. Place chickpeas in saucepan and continue cooking on a low simmer. The pan should be covered slightly or uncovered as needed to fully cook the chickpeas, but reduce the cooking liquor until nearly none is left.

Bring a pot of water to boil for the pasta and salt generously. Meanwhile, saute other half of onion in a dutch oven in a generous amount of olive oil (I use about ¼ cup.) When you begin cooking the pasta, add the tomato paste and garlic to the onion in the dutch oven. Fry tomato paste for 2 or 3 minutes until darkly colored and the olive oil runs red. Then add rosemary, red pepper flakes, and chickpeas with liquor and cooking vegetables. Incorporate everything together and add banana pepper. Raise heat to medium or medium-high and reduce liquid in sauce until very little remains. If you need to keep cooking the chickpeas, you can also keep cooking them and reserve the cooked pasta and its cooking water for the last step. I like the chickpeas to be slightly al dente, because their denser texture provides a nice contrast to the softer pasta.

When the sauce is reduced sufficiently, add in a half cup of the water the pasta cooked in. Make sure dutch oven is over medium-high heat, and incorporate liquid with chickpeas and vegetables. Then, add in pasta, and incorporate thoroughly. Serve with grated cheese if desired.

items: 10 ounces (280g; about 2 cups) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1 teaspoon kosher salt, plus more for salting water

steps: To make the dough: Mound flour in the center of a large, clean work surface, then use your fingers or the bottom of a bowl to push flour out from the center into a wide ring with a 4-inch well in the middle. Crack the whole eggs and egg yolks into the well, then add 1 teaspoon kosher salt.

Use a fork to gently beat the eggs and salt together until smooth, keeping the liquid contained inside the flour well. Continue beating while slowly drawing small amounts of flour from the inner walls of the well into the eggs until a thick, paste-like batter forms and is no longer runny.

Using a bench scraper or your hands, fold the remaining flour into the egg mixture until a shaggy, cohesive dough forms. Clean your hands and work surface of any dried dough bits so they do not get worked into the pasta.

Knead the dough by pressing the heel of your hand into the ball, pushing forward and down, then rotating 45 degrees and repeating. Continue kneading until the dough is smooth, elastic, and has the firm consistency of Play-Doh, about 8 to 10 minutes. (If the dough feels too wet and sticky, knead in flour 1 teaspoon at a time; if too dry and crumbly, mist lightly with water or add a tiny amount of egg yolk.) Wrap tightly in plastic wrap and let rest on the counter for at least 30 minutes (or refrigerate up to 24 hours; bring back to room temperature before rolling).

To roll the dough: Cut the rested dough into quarters. Set one piece on a lightly floured work surface and keep the remaining pieces covered with plastic wrap or a damp towel so they do not dry out. Flatten the piece with a rolling pin into an oblong shape about 1/2-inch thick.

Set a pasta machine to its widest setting and pass the flattened dough through 3 times. Fold both short ends of the dough sheet toward the center so they meet, then fold in half like a book. Flatten slightly with a rolling pin and pass through the widest setting 3 more times.

Narrow the pasta machine by one setting and pass the dough through, repeating the folding and rolling process once or twice until the sheet is smooth and even. Continue narrowing the settings one notch at a time, passing the dough through once or twice per setting without folding, until it reaches your desired thinness (usually the second- or third-thinnest setting for noodles, or the thinnest setting for stuffed pastas). Lightly dust with flour as needed to prevent sticking. Repeat with the remaining dough quarters.

To cut and cook: Cut the rolled sheets to your desired length (about 12 to 14 inches) and run them through the pasta cutter attachment, or loosely roll up lightly floured sheets and slice by hand with a sharp knife. Toss cut noodles with flour, gather into loose nests on a parchment-lined baking sheet, and cover with a clean towel until ready to cook.

Bring a large pot of generously salted water to a boil. Add the fresh pasta and cook until tender yet al dente, about 90 seconds to 2 minutes (a bit longer if dried or frozen). Drain and toss immediately with your sauce of choice.

items: 3 lbs boneless pork shoulder/butt, covered in salt and pepper
Several sprigs of fresh thyme, 1 sprig of rosemary
2 cups white wine, save rest of bottle for later use

steps: Brown pork shoulder in dutch oven, remove, and then pancetta, remove. Preheat oven to 325.

Saute all vegetables, adding garlic and fennel seed at end. Then add tomato paste, holding back if a full tin looks too much, and saute more, adding back pancetta. Add wine, stock, thyme, and rosemary and then the pork shoulder whole. The liquid should go about halfway up the pork.
Brown pork in oven for about 3 hours, adding in more wine or water if liquid levels reduce too much.
Once pork is easily shredded with a fork, remove, and shred, discarding any bones. In the meantime, reduce the sauce if necessary.

Add shredded pork back to sauce with cream, mustard, and parmigiano. Add 1 tsp of orange zest. Orange is very strong so use less at first to not overpower the dish. Cook another 15-30 minutes to bring the flavors together. This is best saved and reheated the following day for even better flavor. Serve with pasta with basil.

items: 1 package dried porcini mushrooms, reconstituted in warm water and chopped

steps: If using, heat ¼ cup oil in a large Dutch oven or other heavy pot over medium. Arrange prosciutto in a single layer in pot and cook, turning once or twice, until crisp, about 5 minutes. Transfer to paper towels to drain.

Heat 2 tbs oil in same pot over high. Cook button mushrooms, tossing occasionally, until browned and tender, 5–8 minutes. Remove from pan and reduce heat to medium-low. Add shallots/onions and 1 tsp. thyme, season with salt and pepper, and cook, stirring often, until shallots are sweet, tender, and somewhat caramelized, about 15 minutes. Add porcini mushrooms and cook for 2 or 3 minutes. Then add stock and cooked button mushrooms and reduce heat to low. Bring to a simmer and cook until only a thin layer of stock coats bottom of pot, 5−7 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water, stirring occasionally, until very al dente, about 3 minutes less than package directions.

Reserve at least 1 cup of pasta cooking liquid. Then drain pasta and add to pot with mushrooms and add the ½ to 1 cup pasta cooking liquid (depending on how much more your pasta needs to cook.) If using, crumble half of prosciutto into pot. Increase heat to medium, bring to a simmer, and cook, tossing constantly, until pasta is al dente and liquid is slightly thickened, about 2 minutes. Add cream and butter, return to a simmer, and cook, tossing, until pasta is coated, about 1 minute. Taste and season with salt if needed.

title: Pasta with Sardines [Pasta con le Sarde]

items: 1 tin of sardines, preferably from Spain or Portugal
½ cup of parsley, fennel fronds, or mixture of both
½ cup of breadcrumbs (I prefer panko and if possible, toast them in a pan with olive oil)
1 lb of spaghetti or similar pasta

steps: Put a pot of water on high heat to boil for pasta. When water is boiling, salt water (it should be almost as salty as the ocean), and put pasta in to cook.

In a high-sided saute or dutch oven (pasta will finish in sauce), saute over medium-low heat in 1 Tbs of olive oil onion and fennel, if using, until onion is translucent and vegetables soft. Add fennel seeds, pepper flakes, and capers and saute another minute. Add sardines, while avoid adding too much oil from tin. Saute sardines until warmed through, breaking them up into small pieces with the back of a wooden spoon. You may have to take this pan off heat at this point if the pasta is not done.

When pasta is almost done, drain, but reserve at least ½ cup of the pasta cooking water. With the sardine mixture over low heat, add pasta directly to pan with reserve cooking water. If using any greens, you should add them at this point as well. Mix pasta and sauce until thoroughly combined and the water is absorbed by the pasta.
Add breadcrumbs and fresh herbs to pasta and toss lightly. Serve immediately.

items: 3 bell peppers (preferably red or a mix of colors but not green), cored and sliced

steps: Saute peppers and onions in a generous amount of olive oil, until they are soft. Add in garlic and continue sauteing. Add in vinegar and combine for 1 minute over heat. Remove from heat and mix in parsley.
Toss everything together and store in an air-tight jar.

items: 3 medium tomatoes, quartered and roughly chopped
1 red onion, halved and thinly sliced
1 bunch of flat leaf parsley, roughly chopped
2 teaspoon ground sumac or more to taste
1 teaspoon paprika or more to taste

steps: Toss everything together. Can add cannellini beans and pine nuts if desired. To be served with feta, olives, pita, and especially kebab.

items: ½ lb of shrimp, shells removed (and reserved if possible)
Half a bunch of scallions, green parts diced
½ lb of penne pasta (or whatever shape you desire)

steps: Heat olive in flat-sided saute pan over medium heat. When hot, add reserve shrimp shells and fry until turning golden. While shells cook, pat shrimp dry, and then toss with 2 tablespoons of cajun seasoning. Season with salt and pepper. Remove shells and then saute shrimp over medium heat in the flavored oil until blackened, about 1 minute each side. Remove shrimp and then add sausage and saute until browned. Once browned, remove. Reserve oil from shrimp and sausage.
Bring a pot of water to boil and cook penne according to instructions.

Add pepper, shallots, and scallions to saute pan with reserved oil. Add a tablespoon of water if necessary and allow liquid of vegetables to begin to deglaze pan. After 5-10 minutes, when vegetables are soft, add garlic and saute 30 seconds. Add cherry tomatoes and saute until warm. Then, deglaze with wine. When wine has almost evaporated add in cream and bring to a simmer. Season with remaining cajun seasoning.

When cream is about to simmer add back in the shrimp and sausage. Bring to a simmer. When pasta is done cooking, reserve ¼ cup of pasta cooking liquid, drain pasta, and then add pasta and liquid to sauce. Add in asiago cheese. Toss together until everything is emulsified.

items: A head or half a head (depending on size) of white, red, or napa cabbage
1-2 Tsp chinkiang or black chinese vinegar (optional)

steps: Place a large saute pan (preferably cast-iron) on medium-high heat and add 2 tablespoons of the oil. Quarter cabbage and then cut across the sides of the cabbage, creating thin ribbons. Once oil is smoking, add in cabbage. The cabbage should be able to spread in an relatively thin, even layer across the pan. Do not stir the cabbage for several minutes, until one side is browned. Begin stirring every minute or so, sometimes giving a side a break, until the cabbage is browned on all sides and it is beginning to lose its moisture.

Add a tablespoon or two of water to the pan and the smashed cloves of garlic. Cook cabbage until water has evaporated and the cabbage is cooked to your taste. If you want the cabbage softer, add another tablespoon or two after the initial water boils off.

Before the last addition of water has completely reduced, add any combination of soy sauces, oyster sauce, vinegar, and [chili oil](recipe:chili-oil) or chili crisp. Toss the cabbage in the pan to spread the sauces evenly over the cabbage.

items: A bunch of carrots, peeled and root ends cut off
A handful of sliced pickled peppers, to taste

steps: Toss carrots with oil and salt and pepper and roast in 400F oven. Toss the carrots on the pan every 5 minutes so that they brown evenly on all sides. When the carrots are browned on all sides and cooked, take out of oven.
Toss roasted carrots with honey or maple syrup and peppers. Top with feta cheese if desired and serve.

notes.name: Note
notes.text: if you don’t have pickled peppers on hand, slice a spicy pepper or peppers (fresno, jalapeno, or anaheim are all good) and let sit with a couple tablespoons of white or apple cider vinegar while the carrots roast. Use the sliced peppers and discard the vinegar (or, better, use for something else, such as a spicy vinegarette.)

items: 1 small jar of green pitted olives
Handful of fresh thyme and/or rosemary sprigs

steps: Heat a braising pot over medium heat and add 1 tablespoon olive oil. Season the beef with salt and pepper generously, toss with flour until evenly covered, and brown all around to sear in a pot. Remove the beef and set aside.

Drain pot of fat, then add another tablespoon of olive oil and the onion, pepper, carrots, and celery. Saute for 5 minutes. Add garlic and tomato paste into the pot and saute for 2 more minutes. Pour in vermouth, stir to get up any browned bits, and reduce.

Once vermouth is reduced to less than half of its original liquid, add tomatoes, olives, marmite, soy sauce, one cup of red wine, and water. Bring to a simmer and then add back in beef along with any collected juices. If the wine from first cup along with the water is not enough to almost cover the beef, then continue to add wine until the beef is almost covered. Season with salt and pepper.

Cover and braise in the oven at 350F for 1.5 hour. After the first hour and a half, remove cover and make sure some of the beef is sticking above liquid. Continue to braise, turning beef over every half hour, so need sides are allowed to roast above the liquid. If liquid reduces too quickly, add more water or wine as desired.
When beef is tender, remove from oven, and strain the sauce through fat separator. Return vegetables minus any herbs to pot with beef with strained sauce.

title: Phil’s Spanish Chicken and Chorizo Stew

items: 8 oz, ½ a package of cherry tomatoes, halved
1 small jar of green pitted olives
Handful of fresh thyme and/or rosemary sprigs

steps: Heat a braising pot over medium heat and add olive oil. Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Brown the chorizo, and then reserve to a plate and then brown chicken starting with skin side first. Remove the chicken and reserve with chorizo.

Drain pot of fat, then add back another two tablespoon of fat and the onion and pepper. Saute for 10 minutes. Add garlic saute for 2 more minutes. Add in the tomatoes, stir to get up any browned bits. Then add in chickpeas, olives, and white wine. Season with salt and pepper.
Once wine is reduced slightly and alcohol is cooked off, add soy sauce, herbs, chorizo, and chicken, nestling the chicken on top of everything else. Bring back to a simmer.

Cover and braise in the oven at 350F for 30 minutes. Uncover for next 15 minutes until liquid is reduced to desired level. Remove from oven and remove chicken thighs from pot. Mix in spinach into stew and then nestle chicken thighs back into stew. Cover and cook another 5 or 7 minutes until the spinach is wilted.

items: 3 and 1/3 cups (about 440g) bread flour (spooned & leveled), plus more as needed for shaping and pan
2 teaspoons instant or active dry yeast
1 heaping cup (about 135g) chopped pepperoni, sun-dried tomatoes (packed in oil & drained), and/or olives
1 and 1/2 cups (360ml) water, close to room temperature at about 70°F (21°C)

steps: In a large mixing bowl, whisk together the flour, yeast, salt, sugar, oregano, basil, garlic powder, and crushed red pepper (if using). Using a silicone spatula or wooden spoon, mix in the chopped add-ins (pepperoni, sun-dried tomatoes, olives) and mozzarella cheese. Pour in the water and gently mix together until all the flour is moistened (use your hands if needed; the dough will be sticky).

Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap or aluminum foil and set on the counter at room temperature. Allow to rise for 3-6 hours until initial proof looks complete. Then, place the covered dough in the refrigerator for at least 12 hours and up to 3 days.

Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured work surface and, using generously floured hands, shape into a ball. Transfer the dough to a large piece of parchment paper, place inside a medium-size mixing bowl or cutting board,, and let rest for 1 hour.
Preheat the oven to 450°F (232°C) 1 hour with a dutch oven inside.
Bake in the preheated Dutch oven or via your preferred method until crusty and golden brown for 30 minutes, covered. Uncover and bake another 10 minutes or until crust has desired browning.

sources.text: Crusty No-Knead Pizza Bread - Sally's Baking Addiction

steps: Combine flour, sugar, salt, and yeast in the bowl of a food processor. Pulse 3 to 4 times until incorporated. Add olive oil and water. Run food processor until mixture forms a ball that rides around the bowl above the blade, about 15 seconds. Continue processing 15 seconds longer. Alternatively, combine ingredients in a stand mixer and mix on low speed for 10 minutes.

Transfer dough ball to a lightly floured surface and knead once or twice by hand until a smooth ball is formed. Transfer to a gallon-sized zipper lock bag, seal, and place in the refrigerator. Allow to ferment for at least 1, and up to 5 days.

At least 2 hours before baking, remove dough from refrigerator and divide into 4 even balls. Shape into balls by gathering dough towards the bottom and pinching shut. Flour well and place each one in a separate bowl (cereal bowls or small mixing bowls work well). Cover tightly with plastic wrap and allow to rise at warm room temperature until roughly doubled in volume.
Meanwhile, adjust oven rack with pizza stone to top position and place a second rack one position below it. Preheat oven to 550°F (290°C, or as hot as your oven will allow) for at least 1 hour.

Turn a single dough ball out onto floured surface. Use a rolling pin to roll it out into a 12-inch circle, lifting and stretching by hand if necessary. Grease an aluminum baking sheet with 1 tablespoon canola oil. Transfer dough to baking sheet. Spread about 1/2 cup of sauce evenly over entire surface of pie. Sprinkle with 1/4 of parmesan. Spread 1/4 of cheese in even layer over surface. Top with additional toppings as desired.

Place in oven on rack immediately under the baking stone. Bake until edges are just beginning to brown, about 5 minutes. Remove from oven (close oven). Using a thin flexible metal spatula, carefully separate the pizza's edges from the pan (the pizza should slide around freely). Carefully slide pizza off of pan and onto baking stone. Continue baking until bottom is deep golden brown and cheese is melted and bubbly. Transfer pizza to a cutting board with a pizza peel. Cut into 8 slices, and serve. Repeat steps 5 and 6 with remaining pizzas.
Whisk together the water, yeast, olive oil, and salt. Let the yeast foam for 5 minutes.

Add in 3 cups of flour and use your dough hook to knead. Knead for a minimum of 5 minutes, until the dough is smooth and just slightly tacky, but not sticky. Add the additional .5 cup of flour, if needed, and knead until smooth. I usually add the half cup of flour to get the tacky texture you want.

Place the dough in a large, well oiled bowl. Cover with plastic wrap and put in a warm place to proof for at least 1 hour, or wrap the dough in plastic wrap and store in your refrigerator until you're ready to use it. If using the dough from the refrigerator, let it come to room temperature before working with it (rest for at least an hour.)
Divide dough into two halves and let each dough ball rest for 20-30 minutes. Stretch, cover, and bake at hottest temperature your oven gets to on a pizza stone or steel!

items: 500 grams (17 ½ ounces or about 3 ¾ cups) all-purpose flour, plus more for shaping the dough

steps: In a medium bowl, thoroughly blend the flour, yeast, and salt. Add the water and, with a wooden spoon or your hands, mix thoroughly.

Cover the bowl with plastic wrap or a kitchen towel and allow it to rise at room temperature (about 72°F) for 18 hours or until it has more than doubled. It will take longer in a chilly room and less time in a very warm one.

Flour a work surface and scrape out the dough. Divide it into 4 equal parts and shape them: For each portion, start with the right side of the dough and pull it toward the center; then do the same with the left, then the top, then the bottom. (The order doesn’t actually matter; what you want is four folds.) Shape each portion into a round and turn seam side down. Mold the dough into a neat circular mound. The mounds should not be sticky; if they are, dust with more flour.

If you don’t intend to use the dough right away, wrap the balls individually in plastic and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Return to room temperature by leaving them out on the counter, covered in a damp cloth, for 2 to 3 hours before needed.

items: 1 or lbs of boneless pork chops or cutlets, pounded to an even thin thickness (~¼ inch or less)

steps: Put flour in rimmed plate (or plate or bowl), beat egg in another rimmed plate, and put a 50/50 mixture of panko and flour (the flour makes the panko adhere and fry more evenly) in rimmed plate, all in a row. Season flour, egg, and panko with salt and pepper (yes all three.) Keeping one hand dry, put each cutlet in flour, egg, and then panko and set aside on a plate.

Heat a high-heat, neutral oil (I use safflower) over medium-high heat. Add cutlets and cook each side 3-5 minutes until coating is nicely browned on both sides and cooked through. Do not crowd the pan, you will almost certainly need to cook cutlets in batches.
Serve with lemon juice and capers or the below beet puree. Either way, they are great with arugula.

notes.name: Chicken Variation
notes.text: Do everything same but replace the pork cutlets with chicken breasts. You can also add hot sauce to the egg for further seasoning. Otherwise, everything is the same.

sections.name: Beet Puree

items: 1 small red beet, peeled, thinly sliced
½ large Granny Smith apple, peeled, thinly sliced
¼ cup plain whole-milk Greek yogurt

steps: Heat olive oil in a small saucepan over medium-low. Cook shallot, stirring occasionally, until soft but without taking on any color, about 4 minutes. Add beet, apple, and broth; season with salt and pepper. Increase heat to medium and bring to a boil; cook until liquid is almost completely evaporated and beets are softened, 15–20 minutes. Let cool 10 minutes, then transfer to a blender. Add cream and yogurt and blend until sauce is the consistency of chunky apple sauce (no large pieces should remain). Season with salt and pepper.

ingredient_groups.name: Pork Ingredients
items: 1 whole bone-in or boneless pork butt (5 to 7 pounds)

steps: Rub the Pulled Pork Dry Rub: Mix all the dry rub ingredients and rub it all over the pork shoulder picnic pieces. Then, put the pork shoulder picnic in the fridge for 30 minutes to overnight.

Brown the Pork Shoulder (See Tips): Add 1 tablespoon of oil into cast iron pan. Ensure to coat the oil over the whole bottom of the pan. Add the pork shoulder pieces into the pot. Brown the pork shoulder on all sides. Remove and set aside. Add onion and scap to pick up browned bits until onion is softened - approximately 5 minutes. Ad ½ cup of water to deglaze.
Put the onion and water in pressure cooker. Add half of the BBQ Sauce and stir to mix together. Add in sprigs of thyme and oregano from garden, if available.

Put browned pork pieces into the pressure cooker. Make sure the skin side of the pork is facing up. Close lid and pressure cook at High Pressure for 75 minutes if bone-in. Turn off the heat and fully Natural Release (roughly 15 minutes).

Fork Tender Check: Open the lid carefully. Take one piece of pork shoulder out and see if you can shred through the meat easily with two forks. If it is not fork-tender, cook for an additional 10 to 20 minutes at High Pressure, fully Natural Release.
Shred the Pork & De-Fat the Sauce: Use some cool Pulled Pork Shredder Claws or two regular forks to shred the pork shoulder meat. Use a fat separator to separate the fat from the BBQ sauce.

Season, Reduce, Serve: Add in the reserved half of the uncooked BBQ sauce to the sauce from the fat separator. Reduce the BBQ sauce to your desired thickness. Taste the BBQ sauce and adjust seasonings. Place the pulled pork back into the BBQ sauce. Mix well and serve!
Serve with reserved BBQ sauce.

items: 1 and 1/2 teaspoons store-bought or homemade pumpkin pie spice
1/4 cup (50g) packed light or dark brown sugar

steps: Preheat waffle maker on medium-high heat. Preheat oven to 200°F (93°C) and place a wire rack on a baking sheet.
In a large bowl, whisk flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, pumpkin pie spice, ginger, and salt together until combined.

In another large bowl, beat eggs on high speed for 1–2 minutes until frothy on top. Add pumpkin, melted butter, brown sugar, maple syrup, vanilla, and milk, and whisk or beat on medium speed until combined.
Pour dry ingredients into wet ingredients and whisk or beat on low speed until combined (do not over-mix; some small lumps are okay).
Grease preheated waffle maker, pour batter into wells, and cook until crisp (about 5–6 minutes). Transfer cooked waffles to the wire rack in the oven to keep warm while cooking remaining batches.

For the optional maple pecan topping, place pecans in a saucepan over medium-low heat and toast for 4–5 minutes until fragrant. Turn heat to low, add maple syrup, warm through for a minute, and remove from heat to serve over waffles.

items: 1 sugar pumpkin, roasted and pureed (see note below) or 1 butternut squash, roasted and pureed
4 garlic cloves, roasted and mashed into a puree
2 ⅓ oz of ricotta or soft blue cheese such as gorgonzola
¼ cup minced sage leaves or (parsley)

steps: Combine roasted squash, garlic, cheese and herbs.
Roll out fresh pasta dough into sheets.

Spoon approximately a tablespoon of the squash mixture in even spacing along a sheet of pasta. Either make several rows and top with another sheet of pasta or fold single sheet and then use pasta cutter to cut into ravioli. Repeat for all pasta sheets. Having extra squash mixture is not unusual.

notes.name: Note
notes.text: This is the best recipe for roasting sugar pumpkins I have found: [https://ohsheglows.com/2012/09/10/how-to-roast-a-sugar-pumpkin-make-fresh-pumpkin-puree-a-step-by-step-photo-tutorial/](https://ohsheglows.com/2012/09/10/how-to-roast-a-sugar-pumpkin-make-fresh-pumpkin-puree-a-step-by-step-photo-tutorial/)

sections.name: Kimchi Quesadillas

items: 1 cup cabbage kimchi, drained and chopped
1 1/2 cup grated Monterey jack and/or cheddar cheese

steps: Sauté the kimchi: Melt 1 1/2 Tbsp of butter in a cast iron (or other relatively stick-free) pan on medium high heat. Add the kimchi and spread out in an even layer over the pan. Cook for 5 to 6 minutes, flipping half way. Remove from pan.

Heat the flour tortilla: Add half of the remaining butter to the pan and swirl it around on the bottom. Add one of the flour tortillas. Add cheese and kimchi: Add half of the grated cheese and half of the sautéd kimchi.

Fold the tortilla over (like an omelette) with a metal spatula. Press down with the spatula. After about 30 seconds or so, flip to the other side. The flour tortilla should be nicely browned.
When the cheese has clearly melted remove from pan and repeat with the other tortilla and the remaining cheese and kimchi.
Serve with sliced avocado and hot sauce, if desired.

sections.name: Kale, Poblano, and Black Bean Quesadillas

items: Leftover taco filling from the [Kale, Poblano, and Black Bean Tacos](recipe:kale-poblano-and-black-bean-tacos), or make from scratch if desired

steps: Same as above, but substitute the kale, poblano, and black bean mixture for the kimchi in the above recipe.

items: 1 cup frozen corn, defrosted, or 1 can of corn
A bunch of greens such as spinach (optional)
1 teaspoon chili powder (chipotle chili powder if available), less or more to taste
1 15 oz. can black beans, drained and rinsed
1 15 oz. can pinto beans, drained and rinsed
1 15 oz. can chickpeas, drained and rinsed
3 cups grated cheddar cheese, divided 2 cups and 1 cup

steps: Cook the quinoa according to package directions. Typically package directions ask you to put 1 cup of quinoa with 2 cups of water and a pinch of salt into a pot, bringing it to a boil, reduce to a very low simmer, cover and cook for 15 minutes. Then remove from heat and fluff with a fork.

Heat olive oil in a large skillet on medium high heat. Add the onions and the bell peppers and cook until softened and browned at the edges, about 10 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin, chili powder, corn, and greens (if using) and cook a minute more. Remove from heat.
Place the cooked quinoa, all three beans, onion mixture, cilantro, and 2 cups of grated cheddar cheese in a large bowl. Toss to combine.
Place in a casserole dish. Sprinkle the top with remaining 1 cup of cheddar cheese, and bake at 350°F uncovered for 15 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly.

items: 4 tablespoons of jerk seasoning, divided in two
1 cup of cream or ½ and ½

steps: Season chicken/shrimp with half of jerk seasoning and then saute in dutch oven or saute pan in olive oil for several minutes until browned.
Remove chicken/shrimp and add all of the vegetables but the garlic and scotch bonnet. Add more oil if necessary and saute until soft. Begin cooking pasta
Add garlic, scotch bonnet, and reserved jerk seasoning as desired. Season with salt and pepper. Add chicken/shrimp back and in and add dairy and bring to a low simmer.
When pasta is finished add to sauce with a ½ cup of pasta cooking liquid. Serve with chopped scallions and/or cilantro.
Into a small pan add your refried beans and cook till completely hot throughout.
In the mean time prepare your sprouts, cilantro, avocado, and tomatoes by washing, and roughly chopping into bite sizes.

Prepare by making tacos with the beans, protein, vegetables, herbs, and avocado.
You can also roast at 400F a butternut squash or sweet potato cut into chunks and tossed with olive oil and chili powder to bulk up the filling.

items: 1 head of cauliflower, cut into florets
1 bunch of kale, ribs removed and chopped
1 bunch of radishes, root ends trimmed and quartered
3-4 tbs capers, to taste, drained and rinsed

steps: Preheat oven to 425F. Put the cauliflower on a foil-lined roasting pan (or sheet pan), toss with at least 2 tbs of olive oil, salt, and pepper, and place in oven. Roast for 20 minutes, flip cauliflower and roast another 20 minutes. If cauliflower is browning/burning too fast while cauliflower roasts, you can bring down the temperature to 400F.
While the cauliflower roasts, toss kale and radishes with sherry vinegar. If you like softer kale, rub it with the vinegar with clean hands to soften it (I don’t do this.)

In a small saute pan, place a ¼ cup of olive oil, garlic, and capers on low heat. You want the garlic and capers to be lightly frying in the oil, but not browning. The oil is done cooking when the garlic should turn golden and the capers slightly wrinkled from frying, about 5-7 minutes. The amount of garlic and capers you use should be determined by how much kale and cauliflower you have - this is the dressing for the salad.

When the cauliflower is done roasting (it should be well-browned on both sides), immediately toss with kale and radishes. The heat from the cauliflower should soften the kale. Toss everything with garlic and caper sauce. Top with dried cherries and serve warm.

sources.text: I make the roasted cauliflower with capers and garlic as a side and wanted to make it into a meal.

items: 2 tins of sardines preserved in olive oil, preferably from Spain or Portugal
½ regular or 1 small red onion, finely diced
¼ cup of tightly-packed parsely, diced

steps: Combine everything and mix together.

items: ¼ cup red beans, dried or canned (see preparation note)
¼ cup chickpeas, dried or canned (see preparation note)
¼ cup lentils (or ¼ cup dried fava beans)
2 large potatoes, peeled and cut into 1-inch cubes
1 bunch beet or Swiss chard leaves
2 fennel bulbs and stalks, washed and chopped
2 cups cubed pumpkin or other squash (zucchini, yellow, butternut, acorn)
4 to 5 stalks wild garlic, garlic scapes, or garlic chives

steps: If using dried beans: Soak beans at least 6 hours, or overnight; drain and rinse.

Peel the fava beans by squeezing each one between your thumb and other fingers. The skins should slip off pretty easily. In a soup pot, simmer beans in water to cover for 45 minutes to 1 hour, adding lentils after 30 minutes. Drain beans and lentils.
If using canned beans: Rinse and simmer beans and lentils in water to cover for 30 minutes, then drain.

For the minestrone: In large soup pot, combine beans with all vegetables in water and bring to a boil. Lower heat to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes. Add fregula and simmer for another 15 minutes.

Note: We just use what canned beans we want, fregula is a Sardinian semolina pasta in pastini shape - we can use anything. The idea is a soup made with fennel, swiss chard, 1 tomato, vegetables, beans, and small pasta. This is a soup appropriate for any season, including summer.
Heat the oven to 450. Put a well-seasoned or nonstick 12-inch pizza pan or cast-iron skillet in oven.

Put the chickpea flour in a bowl; add the salt and pepper. Slowly add 1 cup lukewarm water, whisking to eliminate lumps. Stir in 2 tablespoons olive oil and the rosemary. Cover and let sit while the oven heats, or for as long as 12 hours. The batter should be about the consistency of heavy cream.

Remove the pan, pour 2 tablespoons of the oil into it and swirl. If using, add the onions return the pan to the oven and cook, stirring once or twice, until they’re well browned, 6 to 8 minutes. Stir the onions into the batter.

Immediately pour the batter into the pan. Bake for 10 to 15 minutes, or until the pancake is firm and the edges set. 10 minutes is usually good if your pan has heated sufficiently. The bottom of the pancake should be beginning to evenly brown before moving onto broiling.

Heat the broiler and brush the top of the pancake with 1 or 2 tablespoons of oil if it looks dry. Set the pancake a few inches away from the broiler, and cook just long enough to brown it in spots. Cut it into wedges, and serve hot or warm.
Top with vegetables or cheese, including tomatoes, roasted peppers, goat cheese, or arugula, to make a meal.

title: Spanish Chickpea Spinach Stew (vegan or not) [Espinacas con Garbanzos]

items: 1 14 oz can of chickpeas (drained and washed in colander)
1 Tsp of Spanish smoked paprika, preferably Pimento de la Vera (normal, agridulce, or picante)
1/2 cup of stock or 1 14 oz can of diced tomatoes (or water)

steps: If using sausage, cut sausage into medallions and fry in olive oil until browned on both sides in a straight-sided skillet or dutch oven. Reserve sausage and pour off excess oil, leaving 1 Tbs in pan or dutch oven.

Warm 1 Tbs of olive oil in straight-sided skillet or dutch oven on medium heat and then add onion and saute. If onion begins to burn, add 1 Tbs of water and splash around. Once onion has become translucent and possibly browned in spots (5 minutes), add garlic, and if using, ginger. Saute another 30 seconds. Then add paprika and cumin, if using. Once you can smell the spices, add spinach and wilt (put spinach in in batches if needed.)

Once spinach is wilted, add chickpeas, soy sauce, bay leaves if using, stock or tomatoes, and bring up to simmer. Simmer until a stew has formed and the chickpeas are soft, 15-20 minutes. If using sausage, add sausage in the last 10 minutes or so. Serve warm in bowls.

items: 1 butternut squash, peeled, chopped in half, and sliced in ¼ inch thick half moon slices
2 tbs safflower or other neutral oil
2-3 tsp gochujang (Korean hot pepper paste), or other asian pepper paste such as Chinese broadbean chili paste, to taste

steps: Pre-heat oven to 425F. Thoroughly mix together oils, gochujang, and soy sauce. Line a baking sheet with foil.
Toss squash in a bowl or zip-lock bag with the gochujang sauce until thoroughly coated. Place on baking sheet and cover each piece with a generous amount of sesame seeds. Place in oven.
Roast, rotating sheets once, until tender and browned on some edges, 25–30 minutes.
Place in serving bowl and top with scallions.

items: ⅓ cup grated parmesan/asiago or other hard Italian cheese
1 Tsp red pepper flakes or chili powder
½ Tsp dried Thyme or italian seasoning
1 Tsp hot sauce of choice (carrot-habanero is a good choice)

steps: Pre-heat oven to 350F.

Melt butter in saute pan over medium heat. When butter is melted, add garlic. Saute for 30 second and then add spinach. Toss spinach so that it wilts evenly. When spinach is nearly wilted, add frozen artichokes, and saute until unfrozen and soft. Pour spinach and artichoke mixture onto cutting board and finely chop as desired.

Put cream cheese in microwave safe bowl and microwave until soft and creamy. Add spinach and artichoke mixture and rest of ingredients and thoroughly mix. Season with salt and pepper and place in baking dish. Bake for 30 minutes.

items: 1 jalapeno or other hot pepper, sliced
1 bunch of spring roll rice wrappers

ingredient_groups.name: Peanut Sauce Ingredients
items: ½ cup peanut butter, and/or equivalent or portion of butter made from whole peanuts mashed into nut butter in a mortar and pestle (producing a chunkier texture)
1 lime, juiced, or approximately 2 tbs lime juice
1 tbs, sambal oelek or other chili sauce

steps: Combine peanut sauce ingredients in small and whisk together. Whisk in small amounts of oil until if it has consistency and desired flavor. I usually add 2 to 4 tablespoons.
Prep all of the vegetables. You can add or subtract depending on what you have on hand or want in the spring rolls.

Prepare tofu. First, line a plate with paper towels and place block of tofu on it. Cover with paper towels and press the tofu with a cast iron pan or other heavy object for 10 minutes. Chop pressed tofu into slices or cubes.

Place 3 tablespoons of cornstarch in a large ziplock bag with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce. Add approximately ¼ cup of water or so until a loose batter forms. Add tofu and toss until all tofu pieces are evenly covered by cornstarch batter. Add more cornstarch if necessary to make batter stick to tofu.

Heat up peanut or safflower oil until very hot. Add tofu and fry on all sides until golden. You will probably have to do this in two batches. Drain tofu on paper towel-lined plate. When all tofu has been fried, toss fried tofu with 1 tablespoon of soy sauce and sesame oil.

At dining table have 1 bowl with water to dunk dried spring roll wrappers in. One at time dunk in water until pliable. Then place soaked wrapper on plate and add ingredients. I start with any bigger leafier greens to help hold everything together, then the peanut sauce, then vegetables, then tofu, and, finally, the cilantro and hot pepper slices. Roll spring close and eat. Repeat. Normal dinner is usually 3-4 spring rolls per person.

items: Steaks, I prefer New York Strip Steak
Safflower oil or other neutral, high-heat oil

steps: Thoroughly dry steaks with paper towels. You will probably need two paper towels per steak and aim to get as much moisture as possible. You can do this ahead of time and then store uncovered in a refrigerator to further dry for several hours before cooking. Either way, allow steaks to sit covered in the kitchen at least 30 minutes prior to cooking to bring the steaks to room temperature.
Heat a cast iron pan until very hot. Pour in a generous tablespoon or two of oil, depending on size of pan. The oil should start smoking.
Season steaks with salt and pepper and carefully slide into hot pan with oil.

Cook, 6-8 minutes in total, flipping the steaks often. If you have an instant read thermometer, you want a consistent internal temperature of 125F to 130F for medium. In the last minute, add the butter to the pan (and the herbs if using), and coat the steaks in the butter.
Let the steaks rest covered for 10 minutes, and then serve.

sections.name: Spicy Fennel Steak
steps: Smash fennel seed and mix with red pepper flakes and use that as a rub on the steak. This is great for grilling steaks.

sections.name: Asian Marinade
steps: In step one above, after thoroughly drying the steaks, add them to a large, plastic zip-lock bag. Mix all of the marinade ingredients together and cover the steak. Allow them to sit overnight to 2 hours prior to cooking in a refrigerator. Make sure to take out the bag ahead of time to allow steaks to come up to room temperature. Make sure no garlic or ginger pieces are sticking to the steak and pat dry with paper towels before cooking steaks (they do not have to be completely dry, but there should not be excessive marinade sticking to the steaks.) You should plan on seasoning with much less salt (due to the soy sauce), and you can omit the black pepper if you want.

items: 2 pounds chuck roast, trimmed and cut into 1 ½-inch pieces
1 (14 ounce) can whole or diced tomatoes

steps: Pat the meat dry and season well with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil over high heat in a Dutch oven or heavy-bottom pot. Working in batches to avoid overcrowding, sear the meat until lightly browned on all sides (about 1 to 2 minutes per side). Transfer the browned pieces to a bowl, cover, and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium and add the peeled pearl onions. Cook until softened but not caramelized, about 10 minutes. Add the chopped garlic and cook for 1 more minute.

Stir in the tomato paste, bay leaves, cinnamon, ground clove, and allspice berries. Let the mixture caramelize for 1 minute, then return the meat and any accumulated juices to the pot, stirring to coat.
Pour in the red wine and cognac, using a wooden spoon to scrape up the fond from the bottom of the pot. Simmer for 5 minutes to let the alcohol evaporate slightly.

Add the tomatoes and enough warm water to cover the meat. Reduce the heat to a medium-low slow simmer, cover, and cook until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened (about 1 hour 40 minutes to 2 hours). Stir halfway through, checking to ensure there is enough liquid and adding a bit of hot water if needed.

Adjust seasoning to taste. Remove the bay leaves, cinnamon stick, and allspice berries. Let the stew sit uncovered for 15 minutes before serving warm over orzo, rice, mashed potatoes, or with crusty bread.

title: Tamago Kake Gohan (Japanese-Style Rice With Egg)

items: 1 cup cooked hot white rice (about 12 ounces cooked rice; 340g)

steps: Place rice in a bowl and make a shallow indentation in the center. Break the whole egg into the center. Season with 1/2 teaspoon soy sauce, a pinch of salt, a generous pinch of furikake, 1/2 teaspoon mirin (if using), and a pinch of Hondashi (if using). Stir vigorously with chopsticks to incorporate egg; it should become pale yellow, frothy, and fluffy in texture. Taste and adjust seasonings as necessary. Sprinkle with more furikake, make a small indentation in the top, and add the other egg yolk (if using). Serve immediately.

items: 3 inch knob of ginger, roughly sliced
2 tablespoons Shaoxing wine or Chinese cooking wine

steps: Boil enough water in a large pot/wok or dutch oven to cover the shanks, add the shanks and simmer for 10 minutes. Remove the shanks and clean under running water. Drain the remaining water/thin broth through a sieve into a large enough bowl to hold the liquid.

Heat the oil on medium heat in the large pot/wok. Add onion, ginger, garlic, scallions and fry for several minutes. Add tomato and saute another couple of minutes. Then add tomato paste, broad bean paste, soy sauces, and cooking wine.
Add back in reserved broth/water and the shanks. Add in all of the spices or make a spice sachet for them and then add. Cook the soup on a low simmer for 3-4 hours.
When beef is tender, remove shanks and tear meat into bite size pieces. Strain soup through a sieve, preferably with cheese cloth covering the sieve.

Prepare a bowl with a serving of freshly boiled Asian noodles of choice and bok choy boiled in noodle water. Add pieces of beef and pour in broth to desired amount. Add chopped scallions, cilantro, [chili oil](recipe:chili-oil), and/or spicy Sichuan pickled vegetables such as mustard stems.

title: Thai Noodle Bowls with Tofu and Veggies

ingredient_groups.name: Tofu
items: 2 tbs salted creamy almond, cashew or peanut butter
1-2 tbs maple syrup or coconut sugar
1 dried birds eye chili or chile de arbol, crushed (or sub 1/4 tsp red pepper flake)

ingredient_groups.name: Salad
items: 1 cucumber, halved, seeds removed, and sliced
1 red, orange, or yellow bell pepper, chopped
Half a bunch of fresh cilantro or basil, torn/chopped

ingredient_groups.name: Dressing
items: 1 fresh chili (whatever you prefer), diced, or sub 1/4 tsp red pepper flake
1 tbs maple syrup, plus more to taste
2 tbs rice vinegar (or sub white or apple cider vinegar)

steps: Start by wrapping tofu in a clean towel and setting something heavy on top (like a cast iron skillet) to press out excess moisture for at least 10 minutes. Set aside.

Prepare the tofu sauce in a medium mixing bowl by whisking together 1 tbs sesame oil, almond butter, tamari, lime juice, maple syrup, and 1 crushed chili. Taste and adjust seasonings as needed, adding more tamari for saltiness, lime juice for acidity, chili pepper for heat, or maple syrup for sweetness. Set aside.
Next, prepare rice noodles according to package instructions, then rinse with cold water, drain thoroughly, and set aside.
Prep vegetables next. Set aside.

Prepare salad dressing by adding all ingredients to a small mixing bowl (or jar) and whisking (or shaking vigorously) to combine. Taste and adjust flavors as needed, adding more chilies for heat, tamari for saltiness, lime juice for acidity, or maple syrup for sweetness. Set aside.

Heat a large skillet over medium heat and cut pressed tofu into small rectangles. Toss in 3-4 tbsp cornstarch (they should be well coated) and sauté in 2 remaining tbsp sesame oil, flipping once browned on the underside to ensure even browning – about 5 minutes total. Add the almond butter sauce and stir gently to combine. Cook for another 3-4 minutes, stirring gently to ensure even cooking on all sides. Remove from heat and set aside.

To assemble, divide noodles, vegetables and tofu among serving bowls. Serve with dressing. For more heat, serve with sriracha or chili garlic sauce. Best when fresh, though leftovers keep well when stored separately in the refrigerator up to 3 days.

steps: Combine eggs, lime juice or vinegar, fish sauce, water, and cornstarch in a medium bowl. Beat with a fork until frothy. If the flour forms a few lumps, break up as many as possible with your fingers.
Heat the vegetable oil in a small pot or a round-bottom wok set over medium-high heat until lightly smoking and pour the egg mixture into the oil in one go.

The egg mixture will immediately puff up. Do not disturb it, but shake the pan to make sure the eggs loosen and do not stick to the pan. After 30 to 40 seconds, flip the omelet. There’s no need to keep it nice and round; we want asymmetrical edges. Let the other side cook for another 30 to 40 seconds. Remove the omelet from the pan and serve immediately.

items: 1-2 lbs of vegetables to stir fry, chopped (can be mixture of two vegetables, brussel sprouts, bell peppers, snap peas, mushrooms, spinach, kale, cabbage, and bok choy are all good choices)

steps: Heat oven to 400F. Take tofu out of package and place on top of 2 paper towels on a plate. Cover with 2 more paper towels and place a heavy pan on top (cast iron works well). Let it the pan press the tofu for 10 minutes, changing the paper towels if desired once fully soaked.
Slice tofu in desire pieces. Place on a sheet pan lined with parchment or Silpat. Bake in oven for 25-30 minutes, flipping halfway through, until brown all over.

While tofu is baking, heat oil in wok or pan. When hot, place vegetables in pan. If using more than 1 type of vegetable, stir fry each vegetable separately, adding more oil as needed. Always stir fry leafy greens first.

Before adding baked tofu to pan, add scallions, chilis, or any other small additions to the pan. Let stir fry for 45 seconds, then add baked tofu to pan. Then add sauce to pan and stir continuously for several minutes, until everything is heated through, and the sauce coats the vegetables and tofu.

steps: In a bowl, combine flours and baking powder with salt and pepper. Add a little more than a cup of water and stir to combine; consistency should resemble pancake batter (if batter is too thick, add more water, a little at a time). Stir in the onions, chopped seafood and herbs.

Put a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and film its bottom generously with olive oil. When oil is hot, pour in half the batter until it fills center of pan; spread gently with a spoon to form a large pancake.

Cook about 3 minutes, or until pancake is set around edges; flip pancake and continue cooking for another 3 minutes, then flip it again and cook for another 30 seconds or so, until it is crisp on outside but still moist inside. Remove from pan and serve immediately, while remaining batter cooks.

steps: 1 to 2 days before serving: Make sure the giblets (usually in a bag) are removed from the turkey's cavity. Sprinkle all over with kosher salt, using about 1 tablespoon per 4 pounds of bird, including some into cavities. I do this on a rack in my roasting pan. Loosely cover with plastic and place in the fridge for 1 to 2 days, and until 4 to 5 hours before you want to serve it.

1 to 2 hours before roasting: Remove plastic and discard any juices that have collected around the bird. Allow to come to room temperature, which will take 1 to 2 hours. No need to rinse any salt off the bird; it's all as it should be.

2 1/2 to 3 1/2 hours before serving: Heat oven to 450°F with a rack on the lowest level of the oven. If you plan to stuff the turkey with anything, do so now. Truss the legs (tying them together) with kitchen twine or, uh, any other string you have around.

Toss the onions with a splash of oil (don't worry about seasoning, they'll collect it from the pan) and arrange around the turkey. Combine 1 tablespoon of the melted butter with the maple syrup and chili paste in a small bowl, whisking until smooth. Brush this — or use your hands to coat — all over the turkey, leaving none behind. Here you're supposed to tuck the wings under the bird to prevent the tips from burning, something I have never successfully done, if we're being honest. Have a big piece of foil nearby for when you will want to cover the turkey.
Roast turkey for 25 to 30 minutes, then — this is very important — reduce the oven heat to 350° and continue roasting the bird until a thermometer in thickest part of the breast reads 150 to 155.
Beginning when you reduce the heat, periodically baste the turkey with 1 to 2 tablespoons of the remaining melted butter, and then, when you're out of butter, with the juices from the pan.

This turkey is going to brown fairly quick and quite dark. Don't fret, it will not taste burnt, but go ahead and put the foil on when it gets as dark as you can stand it. Rotate the pan in the oven a couple times, and turn onions in pan over once, for even cooking. Remove the foil for the last 5 to 10 minutes of roasting, so the skin crisps up again.

Rest, carve, and serve: Allow the turkey to rest at room temperature 15 to 20 minutes before carving, which you should estimate 20 or so minutes to do, depending on your comfort level. This will allow the juices to be locked in and the turkey to carry over to an internal temperature of 165°F. Use the rest time to rewarm any sides that need it and to make gravy.

items: 1 cup chopped red onion (about 1 small red onion)
1 bunch of broccoli or 1 small head of cauliflower (about 1 pound), florets removed and sliced into small, bite-sized pieces
5 to 6 ounces baby spinach (about 5 cups, packed)
1 can (15 ounces) black beans, drained and rinsed, or 1½ cups cooked black beans
1 cup shredded Monterey Jack cheese, divided (omit for vegan recipe or use less and substitute nutritional yeast)
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste
Handful of chopped cilantro, for garnishing

steps: Preheat oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit with one rack in the middle of the oven and one in the upper third. Lightly grease a 13 by 9-inch pan with olive oil or cooking spray.

In a large skillet over medium heat, warm the olive oil until simmering. Add the onions and a pinch of salt. Cook, stirring often, until the onions are tender and translucent, about 5 to 7 minutes. Add the broccoli and bell pepper, stir, and reduce heat to medium-low. Cover the skillet (I don’t have a lid for mine, so I just placed a cookie sheet on top). Cook, stirring occasionally, for about 8 to 9 minutes, or until the broccoli is brighter green and just starting to turn golden on the edges.

Add the cumin and cinnamon to the skillet and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add the spinach, a few handfuls at a time, stirring until it has reduced in size. Repeat with remaining spinach and cook until all of the spinach has wilted.

Transfer the contents of the pan to a medium mixing bowl. Add the drained beans, ¼ cup cheese and a drizzle of enchilada sauce (about 2 tablespoons). Season with ½ teaspoon salt and some freshly ground black pepper, to taste.

Assemble the enchiladas: Pour ¼ cup enchilada sauce into your prepared pan and tilt it from side to side until the bottom of the pan is evenly coated. To assemble your first enchilada, spread ½ cup filling mixture down the middle of a tortilla, then snugly wrap the left side over and then the right, to make a wrap. Place it seam side down against the edge of your pan. Repeat with remaining tortillas and filling.
Drizzle the remaining enchilada sauce evenly over the enchiladas, leaving the tips of the enchiladas bare. Sprinkle the remaining shredded cheese evenly over the enchiladas.

Bake, uncovered, on the middle rack for 20 minutes. If the cheese on top isn't golden enough for your liking, carefully transfer the enchiladas to the upper rack of the oven and bake for an additional 3 to 6 minutes, until sufficiently golden and bubbly.
Remove from oven and let the enchiladas rest for 10 minutes (they’re super hot!). Before serving, sprinkle chopped cilantro down the center of the enchiladas. Serve immediately.

items: 3 tablespoons flour (whole wheat flour, all-purpose flour and gluten-free flour blends all work!)
1 teaspoon apple cider vinegar or distilled white vinegar
Freshly ground black pepper, to taste

steps:
This sauce comes together quickly once you get started, so measure the dry ingredients (the flour, chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, oregano, salt and optional cinnamon) into a small bowl and place it near the stove. Place the tomato paste and broth near the stove as well.
In a medium-sized pot over medium heat, warm the oil until it’s it's hot enough that a light sprinkle of the flour/spice mixture sizzles on contact. This might take a couple of minutes, so be patient and don’t step away from the stove!

Once it's ready, pour in the flour and spice mixture. While whisking constantly, cook until fragrant and slightly deepened in color, about 1 minute. Whisk the tomato paste into the mixture, then slowly pour in the broth while whisking constantly to remove any lumps.

Raise heat to medium-high and bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat as necessary to maintain a gentle simmer. Cook, whisking often, for about 5 to 7 minutes, until the sauce has thickened a bit and a spoon encounters some resistance as you stir it. (The sauce will further thicken as it cools.)
Remove from heat, then whisk in the vinegar and season to taste with a generous amount of freshly ground black pepper and more salt, if necessary. Go forth and make enchiladas!

steps: Saute onion in olive oil over medium heat until translucent (about 5 minutes). Add escarole and wilt. Once the escarole has wilted, add garlic and saute another minute. Then add stock and bring up to simmer over medium heat.

Add white beans and any herbs and simmer until beans are cooked through and tender about 15 minutes. Once off heat, add in cheese if desired and stir to evenly incorporate. Serve warm, with a baguette for dipping if desired.

Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps: In a small saucepan set over low heat, melt 1 tablespoon of butter. Add the garlic and cook, stirring for 2 minutes.
Add remaining 3 tablespoons butter to saucepan. When it melts, stir in the lime juice, chili sauce, salt and pepper. Turn off the heat and allow the sauce to rest.

Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil. Add the shrimp and cook for 2 minutes or until they are just firm and pink. Do not overcook. Drain into a colander and shake over the sink to remove excess moisture.

In a large bowl, toss the shrimp and chili sauce. Add jalapeño, if desired, sprinkle with cilantro and toss again. Serves 4, messily. Adapted from Greg Nelson at Doc Ford’s Sanibel Rum Bar and Grille, Sanibel Island, Fla.

steps: Shred the zucchini and onion on the large holes of a box grater or in a food processor with the shredding disk. Alternatively, finely dice the onion in lieu of shredding. Place the shredded vegetables in a colander in the sink and sprinkle with the salt. Toss to combine. Let drain for 30 minutes, then pick up by the handful and squeeze out as much moisture as possible. Place on a kitchen towel or double layer of paper towels.

In a medium bowl, combine the eggs, garlic, cheese, herbs, lemon zest, and pepper. Beat well with a fork. Add the drained zucchini mixture and mix together. Sprinkle the 2 tablespoons of flour and baking powder on top and mix with a fork just until well combined. Keep on adding flour, 1 tablespoon at the time until desired consistency is achieved.

Heat one tablespoon of the olive oil over medium-high heat in a wide, heavy pan. When the oil is hot, drop the batter into the pan by heaping tablespoonful. Cook for about three minutes on the first side, until nicely browned. Flip and cook for about two minutes more. Place the cooked pancakes on a paper towel-lined plate and repeat with the remaining oil and batter. Serve with Greek yogurt, sour cream, tzatziki or soy sauce.

If making vegan, the fritters will be difficult to maneuver in a skillet. Instead of frying, you can placed fritters on a baking sheet and bake for 20-25 minutes in 400F oven, flipping them once midway through. They are ready when both sides are nicely browned and they are cooked through.
Serve fritters with a simple greens salad and sauce, if desired.
